issue: Confluence Apps are not working as intended.
root_cause: In this App, if a Confluence Page does not already have a Classification Level, the level will not be possible to set due to the same issue impacting our other Confluence Apps. The Apps are failing when they try to communicate with the Atlassian Confluence API using the provided resources, which causes an unhandled exception which prevents the App from working - the easiest way to reproduce the problem is when trying to open the Page Byline panels of either App which appear on the top of each Confluence page where the App has been enabled.
solution: The patch for Workflows for Confluence has been deployed and the App functionality should be restored.

issue: Degraded Performance of Translation Memory Component. Introduction We would like to share more details about the events that occurred with Memsource on which led to a partial disruption of the translation memory service and what Memsource engineers are doing to prevent these sorts of issues from happening again.
root_cause: The root cause of the backup failure is identified; the process of deleting corrupted Elasticsearch snapshots starts.
solution: The problematic node of the cluster is manually restarted. The Translation Memory service is disabled to help the Elasticsearch cluster recover by decreasing the number of requests sent to the cluster.

issue: Outage on jessicasuther.land. AEST, an uncached copy of jessicasuther.land was unavailable.
root_cause: This downtime was caused by an accidental policy change to the web property.
solution: We were immediately alerted to this outage by our internal monitoring tools, and deployed a fix within 5 minutes.

issue: Atlassian account session invalidations. SUMMARY a security researcher participating in our bug bounty program notified Atlassian of a vulnerability in our Edge Networking Infrastructure that allowed specially-crafted HTTP requests to interfere with and disrupt the expected handling of network traffic using a technique known as HTTP request smuggling.
root_cause: The root cause was HTTP request smuggling which allowed specially-crafted HTTP requests to interfere with, and disrupt the expected handling of traffic through the load balancers used by Atlassian’s Network Edge.
solution: We have since invalidated all sessions on the affected products.

issue: Authentication Service Outage.
root_cause: Our authentication provider is experiencing an outage, preventing authenticating and logging in to our dashboard.
solution: We will continue monitoring the incident until our authentication provider reports that all functionality has been restored and provide any relevant updates.

issue: INC0034932 - Core link flapping in Reading Data Centre.
root_cause: The root cause of this was a faulty ether-channel on our network, which caused a flapping state and major degradation to some customer services.
solution: The faulty core link has remained stable since service restored. Connectivity has been restored to all affected services.

issue: Homebrew: Security Incident Disclosure.
root_cause: This is due to a flaw in the git_diff dependency of the review-cask-pr GitHub Action, which is used to parse a pull request’s diff for inspection.
solution: We subsequently reverted the PoC pull request, disabled and removed the automerge GitHub Action and disabled and removed the review-cask-pr GitHub Action from all vulnerable repositories. What we’re doing about it The vulnerable review-cask-pr GitHub Action has been disabled and removed from all repositories.

issue: Cloud OMC is not loading properly.
root_cause: After investigation, the issue was due to the Azure host servers rebooting (unplanned) and the OMC startup scripts failed to properly start the backend databases.
solution: To prevent this issue from occurring again due to unexcepted reboots from the host server, we have fixed the startup scripts and are working towards adding more load balancing servers across multiple datacenters.

issue: Our internal engineering team is now prioritizing work that will help ensure reduced impact to customers should such underlying outages happen again.
root_cause: This incident was caused by failures in an underlying MySQL database, which caused some operations to time out for the GitHub Container registry service.
solution: After performing a failover to one of our database replicas, the affected systems were properly restored.

issue: Manage.ntppool.org outage:-/ The ceph storage system hung this morning; the system is slowly recovering (hopefully -- it is still a bit choppy).
root_cause: It took a while (to put it mildly), but we appear to have tracked the trouble down to a recent runc upgrade that'd sometimes get stuck when starting containers.
solution: All has been stable since we downgraded runc.

issue: Degraded performance on getsupport.atlassian.com. We've noticed that getsupport.atlassian.com is responding slowly.
root_cause: We do not have a root cause for the degraded performance impacting the support portal.
solution: The issue has been resolved and the service is operating normally.

issue: Slow Performance. Since rendering a view on the Admin Site requires many database queries, this was most evident on the admin site as pages would be slow to render or only render partially.
root_cause: It took us a few hours to figure out and solve the root cause, so the right thing to do is let you know what was going on behind the scenes. The Background Despite going out of our way to way to make FieldClock appear simple, there’s a lot going on under the surface.
solution: We were able to identify the recalculation catalyst quickly, and we disabled it while we looked at performance. A short while later, we re-enabled our (now fixed) recalculation code so that job numbers would update properly.

issue: Degraded Performance of Editor for Web and Term Base Components. Introduction We would like to share more details about the events that occurred with Memsource on the 12th of May, 2021 which led to the degraded performance of the Editor for Web and Term Base functionality and what Memsource engineers are doing to prevent these sorts of issues from happening again.
root_cause: Not enough heap memory being available to the Term Base Elasticsearch cluster during a rolling restart resulted in a cascade effect and a long recovery time.
solution: Actions to Prevent Recurrence As a reaction to the problems: The size of the Elasticsearch cluster will be increased to provide more overall heap space.

issue: Once the foreign key migration was successful, the internal engineering teams then worked to slowly remove token records stored in our cache layer that were considered invalid.
root_cause: This incident was caused when a foreign key for scoped tokens exceeded max INT32, which resulted in high failure rates for GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages.
solution: We mitigated this with a long-running schema migration to change the foreign key to INT64. After these cached records were removed, newly created API tokens were able to generate new records and API calls resumed working as expected.

issue: Workspot Control Email Services Incident.
root_cause: Starting May 19th, it was discovered that emails were not being delivered from the Workspot service due to a security update at our email provider.
solution: At Workspot Control Service was restarted to enable the security update from our email provider.

issue: Impact to O365 migrations when using Impersonation permissions.
root_cause: Microsoft have provided an update that the fix for this issue is in the process of being deployed to affected tenants at this time.
solution: All indications show that the deployment of the fix has been completed by Microsoft and that this issue has been resolved for our customers. We have had reports where this has been deployed to tenants already and has resolved the issue.

issue: Smart AC Control connectivity issue.
root_cause: We have identified an issue caused by a change from our cloud provider and have escalated the situation to them.
solution: The issue has been resolved, please use Smart AC Control's offline control or use your original IR remote control.

issue: Delays while running CRM integrations.
root_cause: This sudden bump in call volumes was due to the fact that we on-boarded a large number of enterprise clients today but it was totally our fault to not bump up resources allocated for integrations.
solution: Our backlog was cleared and as and when the new calls/texts arrived they were pushed almost immediately.

issue: Web dashboard loading with increased latency. Please note this is just causing a slowdown to loading of the site.
root_cause: The build pipelines have introduced a change which is increasing the asset loading performance of the dashboard.
solution: We recently migrated from Gitlab CI to Github actions.

issue: Problems loading consignments on dashboard. We've finished rolling out the mitigation, and we've seen performance and error rates return to normal.
root_cause: We've resolved the root cause of this issue, and restored the webhook information in the workflow completion page.
solution: As part of the mitigation, we've removed the list of sent webhook messages from the workflow consignment page in the dashboard.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption in North American Region – Web User Interface. at approximately Pacific, the xMatters monitoring tools alerted Customer Support to an issue where the web user interface was unresponsive or exhibiting slow performance.
root_cause: This issue was caused by a single instance attempting to load approximately 140,000 user records into memory. This eventually increased memory usage to 100%, resulting in an unresponsive service.
solution: While the condition properly triggered an automated restart of the web user interface service, the service was unable to recover properly until the underlying issue could be mitigated. The team then manually cleared the cache and restarted the web user interface service, confirming that it had resumed normal operation.

issue: IOS app issue regarding the installation of Smart AC Control devices.
root_cause: A bug in the current version of the iOS app (6.8) prevents users from installing Smart AC Control devices. We have submitted a hot fix App version (6.8.1) to the Appstore and that should be available in the next few days.
solution: The iOS app update (6.8.1) that was released this morning from the App Store has resolved the issue regarding the installation of the Smart AC Control.

issue: Sisense for Cloud Data Teams Database Connection Errors.
root_cause: Starting some Sisense for Cloud Data Teams customers database connections experienced connection errors due to a recent code change.
solution: For these users, a database admin will have to unblock the Sisense user before full functionality can be restored. Engineers rolled back the code are monitoring the connections.

issue: Connectivity issues between Platform and main cluster. The whole process is semi-automated, takes minutes, and results in zero downtime.
root_cause: Our primary server reached a threshold for the “CPU overload” and consequently triggered the CPU overload mitigation process.
solution: While we don’t understand why the Tizen 2.4 system responded in a way that caused the entire device to turn offline (still under investigation), we took steps to prevent this from happening again. As of, most devices are back online, and the issue has been resolved.

issue: Tenat account creation fails. Official response from AWS support: We can confirm increased API latency and increased API error rates for the ACM APIs in the US-EAST-1 Region.
root_cause: Tenant account creation fails due to AWS ACM increased API latency and increased API error rates.
solution: AWS response: We have identified the limit issue and have mitigated it.

issue: Degraded Performance of Project Management, Editors, API and File Processing Components. Introduction We would like to share more details about the events that occurred with Memsource on which led to a partial performance degradation of the Project Management, Editors, API and File Processing services and what Memsource engineers are doing to prevent these sorts of issues from happenin.
root_cause: Newly released functionality caused an overall increase of load on our servers.
solution: Actions to Prevent Recurrence We optimized the code that impacted the performance.

issue: Assignment Canvas Temporarily Disabled.
root_cause: Created automatically as a result of Assignment Canvas entering lockdown mode.
solution: Access to Assignment Canvas has been re-enabled, however users may experience degraded performance for a short period of time. Access to Assignment Canvas has been disabled for all users by an administrator.

issue: JavaScript error prevents notice closing after user choice.
root_cause: The cause for the error was an interaction of a polyfills library (prototype.js v1.7) with our SDK where the polyfills library overloaded the standard JavaScript Array filter method with a non standard findAll function.
solution: The previous version of the Web SDK was restored and deployed back to production on 2021/7/8.

issue: Database connections and PlanetScale dashboard outage.
root_cause: Database connections and the PlanetScale dashboard were unavailable due to a bug introduced in a deploy.
solution: We restored service by rolling back the change.

issue: Intermittent Connectivity Issues. A user who is affected by this incident may experience the AchieveIt application loading slowly or sometimes timing out.
root_cause: Our hosting provider, Microsoft Azure, is experiencing a degradation of their content delivery network (CDN) service that is affecting some AchieveIt users.
solution: As of, Microsoft has reported that it has mitigated the performance degradation on its CDN services.

issue: Degraded performance and increased errors rates. This may also cause some slowness in the dashboard.
root_cause: We've found and resolved the root cause of the issue, and confirmed overnight that the problem hasn't reoccurred. Performance has returned to normal again, and we're continuing to address the root cause.
solution: We've mitigated the effects of the issue, and we're continuing to investigate the root cause.

issue: Mumbai (asia-south1-a) cluster is unavailable.
root_cause: We determined that the root cause was a configuration error introduced during a deployment configuration upgrade.
solution: This was fixed and the cluster was brought back up during a low traffic period at the end of the day. Corrective actions We identified an issue in our CI/CD process that resulted in the initial misconfiguration, which has been corrected.

issue: Random Power Actions API failure & Pings delay. Date 2021-07-12 Authors Lukas Danek, COO / Head of Product Michal Artazov, Lead Developer Summary We experienced degradation in communication between our RabbitMQ “Devices” cluster and its clients.
root_cause: Race condition on the connection endpoint used by devices. Better handling of the connection-loop state management as a part of currently ongoing cluster optimization.
solution: We now have to determine the best way to prevent this in the future.

issue: July 27 incident update. Learn more -> Dismiss July 27 incident update Ryan Dahl Bert Belder Product Update Deno Deploy On Tuesday at several services provided by the Deno organization had a 6 minute service disruption.
root_cause: The issue was caused by a change in our database schema, in which a column got dropped and replaced by another.
solution: We restored service to the deno.land website by redirecting traffic to our backup Cloudflare Workers. At service was restored to Deno Deploy projects.

issue: Controller downtime. The controller was unavailable to service new authentication requests.
root_cause: Leading up to the start of the outage period, automated monitoring alerted us to spikes in memory usage.
solution: Corrective actions seeing the decrease in service availability, we reverted the change and simultaneously made additional hardware available to the cluster.

issue: Azure Connectivity Issue in North American Regions. Between 1345 - 1405 and 1615 – 1635 on August 2nd, customers who were attempting to connect to Azure services may have experienced latency, timeouts, and or connectivity.
root_cause: Azure has reported that they have reverted the network configuration change which established successful connections to Azure services.
solution: The issue is mitigated and no longer impacting customers.

issue: Following ongoing maintenance of the Actions service, our service monitors detected a high error rate on workflow runs for new and in progress jobs, which affected the Actions service.
root_cause: After investigating whether this mitigation would address the incident, we were able to confidently confirm that the bad record was the root cause of the issue, and removing it would restore the Actions service with no unintended side effects.
solution: We immediately reverted recent Actions deployments and started to investigate the issue.

issue: Latency with outgoing email messages.
root_cause: Email messages that are sent by the platform may be delayed due to a malfunction of our service provider. We are working with the service provider and will update when the performance level is back to normal.
solution: Dear Customer, We are happy to advise that the incident with the email latency has been resolved by our email service provider.

issue: Controller downtime. The Controller was partially unavailable to service requests.
root_cause: Leading up to the start of the incident was a planned maintenance period. The maintenance change propagated a configuration change across our Relay clusters.
solution: A hot fix was deployed to the health-check system and it was enabled once again.

issue: Queue system is degraded, slow messages processing. No content playback was affected nor interrupted.
root_cause: The RabbitMQ cluster responsible for communication between devices and system (REST API & Box) has got network partitioned due to some instabilities on network or due to CPU overload during peak of more devices connections.
solution: Devices were shown offline/pending in the Box and the REST API requests were queued until the incident was resolved.

issue: RSA SecurID Access Service Incident (NA Region). Starting at 8/25/2021, three significant and simultaneous events occurred, leading to an authentication outage in NA3.securid.com(.
root_cause: Our cloud provider reported a database outage lasting two minutes. We found three previously unidentified defects in our failure handling.
solution: However, this did not resolve the issue because the restarted nodes were immediately overwhelmed. We reverted software on the affected nodes to the July 2021 release, which allowed us to move the affected customers to a set of servers that was not impacted by these same issues.

issue: Database Server and Site Errors.
root_cause: The 28/08/2021 one of our database servers started to hit a limit on the number of files in a directory - this was caused due to in excess of 22 million individual log files being generated over the course of the last few days, various issues occurred.
solution: The database server was restarted 31/08/2021, and after approx. 20 minutes the database came back online and normal functionality of the sites will have been restored.

issue: Elevated API error rate in Dublin.
root_cause: Traffic to our Dublin infrastructure experienced elevated error rate due to a AWS outage.
solution: The incident started error rate decreased the incident was resolved by We are still performing impact and root-cause analysis, a postmortem with more information will be posted here.

issue: Upstream Connectivity Issue Impacting Service.
root_cause: Our upstream connectivity partner is still seeing unprecedented amounts of traffic ingressing in to the network due to the DDoS attack.
solution: Services have have been restored and we will now close this incident as fully resolved.

issue: Performance Degradation in saas.whitesourcesoftware.com.
root_cause: Thank you, Avinoam Weitman Support Manager Hello everybody, I would like to update that the scan queue was cleared a few hours ago and we have since been noticing a significant improvement in scan processing times, in saas.whitesourcesoftware.com.
solution: Dear Customers and Partners, Following the recurring issue of long scan processing times since August 30th, we have rolled back the changes performed as part of the upgrade to 21.8.1 in our saas.whitesourcesoftware.com environment from August 29th. We're still investigating issue 1, random SAML login failures, and will continue to provide updates until the service has been fully restored.

issue: Summary of AWS Direct Connect Event in the Tokyo (AP-NORTHEAST-1) Region. Engineers attempted several mitigations, such as resetting failed devices and slowly bringing them back into service, but the failures continued and the engineers were unable to maintain adequate healthy capacity to fully mitigate the customer impact.
root_cause: This was caused by the failure of a subset of network devices on one of the network layers along the network path from Direct Connect edge locations to the Datacenter network in the Tokyo Region, where customers’ Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs) reside.
solution: While these devices were not correctly forwarding traffic, they were not being removed from the network through the normal automated processes that monitor and remove failed network devices. Customers started reporting recovery to their applications by JST and by JST affected networking devices were restored to a stable operational state and the Direct Connect service returned to normal operations.

issue: DNS lookup failures. On Thursday, from approximately until our US commercial and government hosting environments both experienced a service interruption related to a configuration error in the service we use to manage our domain name and DNSSEC configuration, GoDaddy.
root_cause: We confirmed with GoDaddy support that they experienced a failure in their managed DNSSEC service that caused some of the regular updates to DNSSEC records to not succeed.
solution: Approximately we cleared the interruption by manually resetting the state on our DNSSEC configuration, and this resulted in queries succeeding across all our monitoring regions within minutes. We observed that the outcome of this failure was that one of RRSIG signing key used to sign the DNSKEY records for the achieveit.com domain was not properly rotated and thus expired September.

issue: Raising Tickets in the Self Service Portal and Email To Ticket. At a few customers reported issues with logging tickets in the Self Service Portal and we very quickly narrowed this down to the software release and this issue also impacted the Email To Ticket service for a a small number of customers.
root_cause: The issue relating to email processing and logging tickets via the Self Service Portal were related to a software update that was performed earlier that morning.
solution: All customers were rolled back to the previous software version and this resolved the issues that affected those customers.

issue: Performance-related slowdowns.
root_cause: Customers were experiencing periodic slowdowns due to insufficient API server capacity caused by some recent capacity changes.
solution: Server capacity has been increased which resolved the problem.

issue: Partial Degraded Performance of Project Management, Editors, API and File Processing Components. Introduction We would like to share more details about the events that occurred with Memsource on September 14th, 2021 which led to a partial performance degradation of the Project Management, Editors, API and File Processing components and what Memsource engineers are doing to prevent thes.
root_cause: The number of slow queries on the database server went up in a short amount of time.
solution: Actions to Prevent Recurrence Enhance monitoring of the database to trigger earlier warnings.

issue: Qoreportal and LicensePortal may not be available. QorePortal was temporarily unavailable and a new cluster was created.
root_cause: The root cause is not clear for sure, but it is related to overlap KeyVaults issue and POA Windows updates.
solution: This update, all Service Fabric nodes are restarted. And the nodes with these applications had to be restarted.

issue: Delay in Trace Processing.
root_cause: Due to a failed hardware node processing of traces is currently delayed for a few minutes. We expect this to be fixed by our hoster in a few minutes and will update you.
solution: However the hardware node has failed and needs to be restarted from a backup.

issue: RSA SecurID Access Service Incident (NA Region). an authentication outage occurred that lasted 1 hour and 12 minutes.
root_cause: The primary root cause of the issue was a change in the configuration of our virtual machines that was put in place after an outage on September 12 but that did not perform sufficiently.
solution: The upgrade process, the front-end CPUs hit maximum load and only recovered when they were restored to the July release. Recent internal changes removed regular and recurring load spikes but raised the average traffic load between server nodes by a significant percentage.

issue: September 23 incident update. Learn more -> Dismiss September 23 incident update Luca Casonato Product Update Deno Deploy On Thursday at several services provided by the Deno company had a 35 minute service disruption.
root_cause: Deno Deploy has a primary Postgres database that is hosted on Google Cloud Platform.
solution: The database server restarted automatically due to the earlier failure, and the alarm was cleared. After the maintenance event ended, the database server restarted automatically, and all services that were using the primary database were able to recover.

issue: Short Degraded Performance of Project Management, Editors, API and File Processing Components. Introduction We would like to share more details about the events that occurred with Memsource on September 26th, 2021 which led to a partial performance degradation of the Project Management, Editors, API and File Processing services and what Memsource engineers are doing to prevent these is.
root_cause: The number of slow queries on the database server increased in a short period of time.
solution: Actions to Prevent Recurrence Enhance monitoring of the database to trigger earlier warnings.

issue: Users are unable to sign in to MURAL. The outage resulted in 50 minutes of downtime.
root_cause: This in turn overloaded the database and resulted in access requests also failing.
solution: Once the original operation finished the database returned to normal operations and access to the MURAL application was restored.

issue: Intermittent access errors.
root_cause: Yesterday were caused by automated updates happening on one of our database servers. These updates are normally configured to automatically complete out of hours - however, a failing update caused a delay in this.
solution: In order to resolve this, we manually failed over writes to DB3 which restored some partial functionality until it was again overwhelmed with queued requests. In order to prevent this from happening again, we have disabled the automatic rescheduling of failed updates outside of the approved windows.

issue: StoryCorps.org temporarily down due to vendor outage.
root_cause: Due to a vendor outage, multiple StoryCorps sites (including StoryCorps.org and StoryCorps DIY) are currently experiencing downtime.
solution: We'll provide an update once this is resolved by the vendor.

issue: Service Alert - WileyPLUS Vitalsource Issue.
root_cause: Our eText vendor, VitalSource is experiencing performance degradation that it impacting access to the eText from WileyPLUS.
solution: We are pleased to report that the previous issues WileyPLUS was experiencing have been resolved, and VitalSource has signaled that the issue is cleared.

issue: Gradual Degraded Performance of Project Management Component. Introduction We would like to share more details about the events that occurred with Memsource on September 30th, 2021 which led to a gradual outage of the Project Management component and what Memsource engineers are doing to prevent these issues from happening again.
root_cause: An unnoticed programming error combined with an error in the build process led to the deployment of an incorrectly built user interface to some production servers.
solution: All servers with the new version of the system are disabled resolving the problem for all users: All servers are rolled back to the previous version of the system.

issue: Degradation of Hosted Email Services.
root_cause: Our third party partner has reported customers experiencing degradation in service of Hosted Email (Inbound/Outbound Mail, IMAP, POP3).
solution: The issue has been resolved and all services are fully operational.

issue: Calling Services: Multiple Feature Servers. HTDNET Support Hello Valued Customers, At approximately Wednesday 10/6, in order to mitigate the disruptions from a DDoS attack; HTDNET's Network Services Team applied a change to our network security devices at the recommendation of our vendor.
root_cause: This is due to the necessary implementation of a network change that slightly reduced usable packet size. Cloud Services and Support are working on reducing the packet size on these outbound dial invites.
solution: HTDNET Support Hello Valued Customers, The DDoS attack that hit HTDNET’s network yesterday has subsided and our services have been restored. Customers may still experience a variety of network related symptoms including portal down or slow, voice quality, dropped calls and unable to make or receive calls until services have completely restored.

issue: SSL issue on tribe.so subdomains. We have experienced 18 minutes of downtime on V1 communities under tribe.so subdomain and some V2 communities.
root_cause: The root cause of this issue was expiration of an intermediate SSL certificate.
solution: Our engineers identified the issue right away and patched the servers with an updated intermediate SSL certificate.

issue: Notarize application: degraded performance related to meeting starts and notary functionality. Notarize application is experiencing degraded performance and increased error rates in the functionality related to RON meeting starts and notary functionality.
root_cause: The engineering team found the root cause of today's meeting performance problems.
solution: We can confirm that short term capacity increase mitigated this issue fully today.

issue: Degraded Performance of All Memsource Components. Introduction We would like to share more details about the events that occurred with Memsource on October 7th, 2021 which led to a partial performance degradation of all Memsource components and what Memsource engineers are doing to prevent these issues from happening again.
root_cause: Processing of complex queries in a new version of the database cleaner created large temporary database tables on a database volume dedicated to creating such tables.
solution: Thu 7th October: Some servers are reconfigured to disable unnecessary database requests to decrease the database load; Memsource engineers continue looking for the root cause.

issue: Gradual Degraded Performance of All Memsource Components: Slow Project Management affects the responsiveness of other Memsource components.
root_cause: The database server was close to the configured global query capacity when incoming user requests triggered many high performance database queries.
solution: High database load is identified as the cause of slow responsiveness; some servers are reconfigured to disable unnecessary database requests to decrease the database load.

issue: Cloud Mail Web App Unavailable. Mail delivery is not affected, so incoming mail will be delivered to your mailbox, even if you are temporarily unable to sign in.
root_cause: The Web App is online again, but it may take a few seconds longer than usual to sign in, due to the combination of Monday morning traffic and extra sign in traffic, since all mailboxes were automatically signed out during the upgrade.
solution: Engineers resolved this incident monitored it throughout the day. We expect services to be fully restored before Noon on Monday October.

issue: Internet service disruption. This was a state-wide outage which affected multiple ISPs in Queensland.
root_cause: The fault was due to a power failure on an interstate connection, which affected a number of fibre-optic nodes.
solution: Customers with LTE backup services automatically switched to these links for internet access.

issue: Issue with Pay API. We take platform availability very seriously and are sorry for the impact this outage had on your users and service teams.
root_cause: On Friday 22 October 2021 for a 16 minute period between -BST, the Pay platform experienced severely degraded availability of our Public API due to the failure of a Redis node used to enforce rate-limiting.
solution: Service was restored by automated processes within 16 minutes. Due to the nature of cloud services, sometimes an underlying machine instance will have a hardware failure, or need to be upgraded or shut down for maintenance.

issue: San Diego Aging Lab - Network Outage.
root_cause: We have identified that the issue regarding the internet outage stemmed from a tripped circuit breaker, and we have reset the circuit.
solution: After a day of monitoring and investigation, we are confident that the issue has been resolved and everything should work as normal.

issue: Heroku SSL Service Degradation. Unfortunately, if your agent was "locked out" from an expired authentication and was unable to report data during the outage, those unreported data will not be available for view on the dashboard.
root_cause: Due to the nature of the incident and it requiring updating our DNS records, it may take some time to fully resolve.
solution: We believe most customer agents have resumed normal reporting and the issue has been resolved.

issue: Controller downtime. This failover process resulted in a partial outage of the Controller, which was partially available to service requests.
root_cause: A physical hardware failure occurred in a single node within one of our Eastern US Relay clusters.
solution: Connectors and Clients attached to this node automatically failed over to a new node.

issue: Frame service outage across multiple regions.
root_cause: The root cause was related to how some of our more recently updated backend services were affected by the US daylight savings time change. Note, that users already in sessions at the start of the incident were not affected by this issue.
solution: We have resolved the issue and users can now start new sessions again and admin access to the affected Frame Dashboard pages has been restored.

issue: Bulldax EOS 출금 일시 중단 안내(재개 완료) / EOS withdrawal suspended.
root_cause: Currently, due to the EOS network issue, Bitgo has temporarily suspended EOS withdrawal support.
solution: Suspension of EOS withdrawal -Suspension period: p.m.-until completion -Suspended contents: Suspension of BITGO withdrawal support due to EOS network issue We will continuously try our best to provide the best service for all our users.

issue: Web App is Unreachable. Both conditions were necessary for the Web UI to become unavailable.
root_cause: What we are doing to prevent it from happening again: We expect both necessary conditions – the failure of the network management software and that the web service was running on a single node be resolved by an already planned migration of our entire service to a new cloud-based environment.
solution: Later, we restarted the unreachable node, which restored it to normal usage.

issue: Loss of connectivity to third party carrier.
root_cause: Nov 15, - Upstream carrier is reporting that the outage was caused by a number of severed fiber lines due to the landslides in BC.
solution: Services are currently being restored and their senior engineers are monitoring the services as they come back online.

issue: Service provider networking outage. Twingate services were unavailable to service requests on November 16th.
root_cause: Google Cloud Platform (GCP) deployed a configuration change in their infrastructure that caused all requests to return 404 errors (GCP incident description).
solution: GCP confirms that the incident was resolved as of. While traffic was being restored, systems indicated that Connectors did not automatically recover.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption in All Regions – Multiple Services. For the duration of the incident, users were unable to access the web user interface, incoming signals were not processing, and notifications were not being generated.
root_cause: Preliminary analysis, the root cause of the issue was a latent bug in a network configuration service which was triggered during routine system operation." See for the complete report from Google.
solution: The incident team remained engaged until Google resolved the incident to ensure that xMatters recovered smoothly once services were restored. There was no intervention required after Google resolved the issue, but some customers may have experienced slow loading times until all Google networking components fully recovered.

issue: HintOS temporarily unavailable - RESOLVED. Hint’s API web-servers stopped responding, causing a 24 minute complete application outage for Hint’s customers and partners.
root_cause: They determined that the root cause was a rare race condition that we encountered in their recently upgraded deployment process.

issue: Performance Disruption of All Memsource Components. Memsource is operational but may be slower for some users.
root_cause: In all cases the root cause was similar: some project related queries were overloading the capacity of the database server.
solution: Affected servers are restarted to free up used memory and reclaim DB connections: The API user overloading the system is identified and the API manually disabled for the user.

issue: SSL certificate error preventing access to web application in US Government environment. This interrupted the service for most customers using the system in our US Government environment.
root_cause: We use an automated process to update the SSL certificate for each service as that certificate approaches its expiration.
solution: We remediated the problem by manually updating the SSL certificate and by all service was fully restored. We also corrected the missing permission to ensure that future automated certificate renewals are propagated successfully.

issue: Degraded Performance of the File Processing Component. Introduction We would like to share more details about the events that occurred with Memsource on November 29th, 2021 which led to a gradual outage of the Project Management service and what Memsource engineers are doing to prevent these issues from happening again.
root_cause: A large number of asynchronous requests sent in a short period of time by a customer’s broken integration significantly degraded the performance of the File Processing service.
solution: Actions to Prevent Recurrence A per organization limit on the number of concurrent asynchronous requests was introduced.

issue: 502 Errors. This resulted in the 502 errors seen, and other disruption to the Wordpress Cluster.
root_cause: Unfortunately by the time the network disruption had subsided - the cluster was unable to recover due to the number of connections being held open waiting for the outcome of changes to the database.
solution: In order to resolve this, we shutdown the database cluster, cleared all open connections held through our webservers and then brought the database cluster up one node at a time, using the most up to date node to prevent data loss.

issue: Long response times & Delayed Log-in on Hydrow. Slow response times and delays on Hydrow have continued intermittently as Amazon Web Services continues their attempts to mitigate their outage.
root_cause: The Amazon Web Services outage has been clearly identified as the root cause of this issue. They are working to fully restore service but Hydrow response times remain slightly degraded.
solution: Amazon Web Services has mitigated the issue that was causing problems for Hydrow services.

issue: Notifications - Degraded performance.
root_cause: Notifications are experience slower-than-normal performance issues due to an issue with AWS.
solution: The incident impacting AWS has been resolved, and as a result our Notifications performance has been restored.

solution: Dec 28, we have investigated the root cause and the issue was fixed. Dec 28, we have restored the unintentionally unlinked associations.

issue: Error rates in all Amazon S3 datacenters began to quickly climb and our alarms went off.

solution: All server-to-server communication was stopped, request processing components shut down, and the system's state cleared. we'd restored internal communication between all Amazon S3 servers and began reactivating request processing components concurrently in both the US and EU.

issue: Cloudflare outage on Cloudflare outage on Loading.
root_cause: An incorrect ordering of the disabled BGP advertised prefixes caused malfunction on 19 datacenters.
solution: The first data center was brought back online and by all data centers were online and working correctly.

root_cause: Private tokens were leaked, and allowed attackers to retrieve data, both in internal databases, in private repositories and from customers accounts.

issue: Processing delays on 422272. Investigation into the throughput showed acknowledgement slowness.

From the December 27th, 2021, there were sporadic delays of processing between 2SMS and its upstream provider Sybase.
solution: These configuration changes, 2sms also made use of an idle process restarter to ensure that if for whatever reason our connection to our supplier stopped processing traffic, our service would be automatically restarted to reduce downtime of processing. issue: January 4th incident update. Learn more -> Dismiss January 4th incident update Kitson Kelly Product Update On January 4th at for about 40 minutes, modules available on deno.land/x and deno.land/std failed to load properly.
root_cause: deno.land/x and deno.land/std served code wrapped in an HTML user interface to run-times, instead of the plain code. The code was refactored to provide more complaint content negotiation, but did not account that run-time clients like the Deno CLI and Deno Deploy provide an Accept header in requests that indicates that all content types are acceptable, including text/html, therefore the code served HTML to those clients.
solution: This post details what exactly happened and what we are doing to prevent this in the future. At the code was amended again to refer to an earlier deployment of deno.land directly for the dependencies, which allowed the code to be deployed and restored service.

issue: Error on our DED-EU1 server. While restarting all services we also used the downtime to update the MTN Media Cloud to the newest version.
root_cause: Due to these issues the MTN Media Cloud was temporarily unavailable. The issue could quickly be found in a php version mismatch on the server which was fixed by reinstalling the required php version and restarting all services.

issue: Retrospective and Technical Details on the recent Firefox Outage - Mozilla Hacks - the Web developer blog Retrospective and Technical Details on the recent Firefox Outage By Christian Holler Posted on in Featured Article, Firefox, and Firefox OS On January 13th 2022, Firefox became unusable for close to two hours for users worldwide.
root_cause: On January 13th, 2022, a specific code path in Firefox's network stack triggered a problem in the HTTP/3 protocol implementation. This blocked network communication and made Firefox unresponsive, unable to load web content for nearly two hours.
solution: For those services hosted on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) these load balancers have settings related to the HTTP protocol they should advertise and one of these settings is HTTP/3 support with three states: “Enabled”, “Disabled” or “Automatic (default)”. This is why users who disabled Telemetry would see this problem resolved even though the problem is not related to Telemetry functionality itself and could have been triggered otherwise.

During post-setup fine-tuning it was identified that initial values for the read capacity units (RCUs) and write capacity units (RCUs) were over-provisioned.
