root_cause: During the load test, the Deno Deploy infrastructure scaled up automatically to handle the increased load.
solution: When the load test was over, the infrastructure scaled back down.

issue: Log lines not ingested. During that time, newly submitted logs were never ingested and therefore not available for Alerting, Searching, Live Tail, Graphing, Timelines, and Archiving.
root_cause: Because of this versioning mismatch, logs from the ingester stopped being accepted by a downstream service (the “buzzsaw broker”).
solution: We manually reverted our ingester service to an older version (to solve a minor problem unrelated to this incident). During the procedure, the version of the container was reverted, but not the container’s configuration.

issue: Newly uploaded files are returning 403 from files.pythonhosted.org. The result was that newly uploaded files as well as files that had expired from our CDNs cache were unavailable.
root_cause: Due to the caching nature of our CDN, it was not detected that this error was occurring as the file checked never expired from cache.
solution: The outage began 2022-06-022 and was initially mitigated 2022-06-02 by rolling back the configuration to a previous version. The configuration issue in the hosted platform was confirmed and corrected 2022-06-02 and a corrected new version of the CDN configuration was deployed.

issue: Twingate Controller outage.
root_cause: After a detailed investigation, we found that during the upgrade, network connectivity between internal components was not stable, triggering failures and retries.
solution: We downgraded our active clusters node pools to the previous Kubernetes version. This added extra capacity and then we failed back to our active cluster.

issue: Ionic Zendesk support issue. Users may be unable to access the ticketing system or KB until the problem is resolved.
root_cause: The Ionic ticketing system and Knowledge Base are affected due to an issue with our Zendesk instance.
solution: We anticipate some delays when the service is restored to clear any backlog.

issue: Redirect Loops on JSON API endpoints. The redirect updates specifically had an unintended consequence that led to this outage.
root_cause: Because of the massive scale of PyPI's caches it was untenable to specifically purge bad URLs, leading to a need to clear the entire PyPI cache.
solution: While the purges were ongoing PyPI's backends even in a scaled out state provided lackluster response times and performance as the caches were slowly refilled.

issue: Customer Conversations Not Successfully Migrated to Messages.
root_cause: We've fixed the root cause so we expect this issue should not impact any customers moving forward. We are now re-migrating the conversations for all previously impacted schools.
solution: We have re-migrated the conversations for all impacted schools and are monitoring to make sure everything is fixed.

issue: Some users are unable to access their murals. On June 14th we started to receive isolated reports of MURAL users in Europe being unable to access their murals.
root_cause: This was confirmed to be the root cause of the issue affecting MURAL users. in collaboration with our cloud provider, we successfully updated our connection to the Azure portal.
solution: Full connectivity and service in MURAL had been restored.

issue: Customer portal outage. We're investigating an outage with our customer portal app.abusix.com.
root_cause: Two of our external providers Auth0 and Cloudflare report incidents with their systems.
solution: The two providers report that they resolved the issue.

issue: Connection issues across all websites. None of the engineers were awake during the outage, so we were not able to post a incident here.
root_cause: This outage seems to be caused by issues on our upstream provider, Cloudflare.
solution: Traffic seems to be stabilized for now and CloudFlare's statuspage states that the issue has been fixed.

issue: Disruption to Indicator Risk Scoring.
root_cause: As part of our product release during the morning of June 20th, there was an update to an external library used by our risk scoring code.
solution: Friday, June 24th - By 2pm, all domain risk scores and most IP and URL risk scores were corrected. Risk scores related to affected hashes and other entities were still being reprocessed.

issue: Loss of tabular data content on certain web pages.
root_cause: Following the migration from the previous version of the content management system our website uses, it was identified that content pages using table data from a specific field type were missing and not appearing on various pages.
solution: This data was not migrated correctly and unfortunately not detected during the live migration before enabling the new production environment.

issue: Increased 502 responses to our Core API.
root_cause: We believe this is due to a recently introduced piece of code that is consuming more memory than it should be and are working on a fix.
solution: We have deployed a fix and are monitoring our container memory consumption.

issue: Queue delay affecting CDN purges and emails.
root_cause: PyPI initially experienced delays in features which used a centralized task queue (such as purging the CDN cache and sending emails) due to a poorly performing task type.
solution: On Sun, 26 Jun 2022 PyPI admins deployed an unrelated change which replaced the JSON serializer used by PyPI from the standard library JSON serializer to a third-party JSON serializer, with benchmarks indicating that this would result in a 6x savings on time to serialize JSON, and thus a significant savings on response time for PyPI’s various JSON-rendering endpoints. PyPI admins deployed the first change that disabled the 2FA metrics task, which resulted in stopping additional long-running queries from being created.

issue: Errors when trying to check users. Without a cache storage, Dangerous Discord would not work at all, and the reason is that the cache stores all user information such as username and avatar.
root_cause: 19.27 - We identified that our config file is broken, and a full reinstallation of Redis is required. 19.37 - Redis has been reinstalled fully again; Changed cache traffic routing to our primary server again.
solution: 19.14 - Latest version installed, we restarted Redis which caused it to throw an error.

issue: Slow and failing Agent chart data responses. Users with nightly versions of the Netdata Agent are experiencing slow responses between Cloud and Agent, resulting in failing or slow charts in their Cloud dashboards.
root_cause: In the mean time we've also found the true cause: the Agent was not properly processing incoming commands in the MQTT5 implementation, due to a bug in how the parser interacted with the buffer of incoming data.
solution: Reverting the default away from MQTT5 removed the immediate issue, and most Agents on the nightlies are now on the latest (v1.35.0-104-nightly). Latest, corrected version is v1.35.0-104-nightly.

issue: Some customers' logs are not currently being processed.
root_cause: We inadvertently released code into production that contained a bug in the parser service. This bug was known to us and in the process of being fixed in our development environment, but was not yet ready for release to production.
solution: The log lines were successfully accepted by our ingestion service, but a downstream service – the parser – removed some of them. This included exclusion rules made by customers in the past and then disabled.

issue: Office 365 - Some users may experience delays when sending or receiving email messages. User Users may have experienced intermittent delays when sending or receiving email messages in Exchange Online.
root_cause: A section of infrastructure, responsible for email attribution and routing, unexpectedly became unresponsive and resulted in DNS lookup failing to resolve hostnames.
solution: Some users may still experience delays whilst services are being restored. We've rerouted user traffic to alternate infrastructure which restored the mail flow delays and remediated impact.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption in North American Region – Web User Interface. at approximately Pacific, some customers in North America reported an issue to xMatters Customer Support where they were unable to load User and Group Performance reports.
root_cause: The issue was traced to enhancements to the User and Group Performance reports that had been enabled, or toggled shortly before the first reported issues.
solution: This allowed the web user interface to more easily complete its processing requirements and the backlog of requests quickly cleared. Customers confirmed that performance had returned to normal levels and service had been restored.

issue: July 13th Utah Outage Update. July 13th Utah Outage Update | Deno Skip to main content Deno is joining Cloudflare!
root_cause: End user requests entering the Deno Deploy network go through various load balancers before ultimately ending up at a service that can execute JavaScript code to respond to the request.
solution: On July 15th, at the load balancer entered the same faulted state as before, and we again disabled the region. The region will remain disabled until our monitoring has improved and the issue has been fixed more permanently.

issue: 2022-07-18 incident update. Learn more -> Dismiss 2022-07-18 incident update Kitson Kelly Ryan Dahl Product Update Deno Deploy Starting on July 18th at all Deno Deploy services (including subhosting) experienced an service disruption until approximately (65 minutes).
root_cause: The root cause was that the etcd instances hit their storage quota limit.
solution: The cluster was successfully rebuilt and services start to come back online at about.

issue: Orion Command Center: Groups and Dispatch Functionality - Partial Outage.
root_cause: The outage was caused by an unexpected spike in traffic which caused the degraded performance of our systems.
solution: The issue has been resolved and a fix has been implemented.

issue: Ingestion and web UI outage. Action was taken to restore the service in a degraded mode, which recovered the Lightstep UI.
root_cause: Lightstep UI and Data Ingest experienced an outage triggered by a planned database change on July 21st.
solution: A subsequent roll back of the database change restored all systems and services. Incident resolved, status page updated to “mitigated and monitoring”.

issue: Failing to ingest some span data.
root_cause: This backpressure led to resource exhaustion in one fleet of span ingestion pods, which caused a partial failure to ingest span data.
solution: The issue was resolved by scaling up the ingest pool.

issue: SecurID Service Incident (EMEA Region). authentication services hosted in the EU region were degraded for 1 hour and 40 minutes (from ET to ET).
root_cause: The incident occurred due to a failure with our cloud service provider affecting our EU West deployment. SecurID CAS systems in this region lost connectivity to backend Database services hosted by our cloud provider.
solution: Microsoft was able to mitigate the incident in EU West, which restored the Authentication service, before we could complete the DR failover procedures.

issue: We applied temporary mitigations, including scaling up our VM pools to absorb the high failure rate, as well as adjusting timeouts to accelerate failure for VMs that were unlikely to succeed.
root_cause: The rate of codespace creations and starts on the 2-core and 4-core machine types exceeded the rate of successful VM creations needed to run, which eventually led to resource exhaustion of the underlying VMs.
solution: This incident, a subset of codespaces in the East US and West US regions using 2-core and 4-core machine types could not be created or restarted. the pools for 2-core and 4-core VMs were drained and unable to keep up with demand, so we statused yellow.

issue: Partial System Outage. Normally this would not cause any disruption as all our systems are in a high availability configuration.
root_cause: The issue on the 27th July 2022, where some customers experienced intermittent system outages, was caused by a hardware failure with one of our servers.
solution: The configuration issue was corrected restoring full service to all customers and we are conducting a full review of all configurations, processes and procedures.

issue: PyPI Outage. PyPI experienced an outage in its backends from 2022-07-28.
root_cause: This outage stemmed from a cascading failure in the backend infrastructure that disrupted the management layer that deploys and secures PyPI's application servers.
solution: Details Beginning at multiple cloud instances that are members of the Kubernetes cluster that PyPI runs on were automatically replaced by the provider due to an unknown failure. By all instances were replaced and healthy as part of the Kubernetes cluster.

issue: Notice: PyPI Mass CDN Purge. Error rates have returned to baseline, and latencies continue to return to normal across our services.
root_cause: In order to resolve an issue in our CDN cache caused by a misconfiguration of Surrogate-Keys, PyPI will need to issue a "Purge All" of our CDN to clear out lingering cached objects that are not accessible to purge individually.
solution: The peak of the backend traffic from our CDN we recognized a few bottlenecks in our database layer and have provisioned additional storage IOPs in order to reduce impact of surges in the future.

issue: Intermittent Login Problems Remediated. We experienced intermittent site login and app/integration related issues this morning.
root_cause: Our investigation, we found that certain combinations of specific rule filters and actions caused conflicts on the servers handling those requests.
solution: We immediately mitigated the issue and deployed additional server capacity as a buffer.

issue: Degraded Platform Performance | Third Party. We are experiencing slower than usual loading times for our website and apps.
root_cause: This is due to one a service provider currently experiencing an outage.
solution: Rostering features and workflows have been restored.

issue: Web: Login non functional.
root_cause: Workers are behind in processing due to the outage and data is not ingested in real-time at the moment. We are rolling out a small configuration change to get a few services back up and running.
solution: We performed a fail-over to backup hardware and the service has been restored.

issue: Issue with AbuseHQ instance settings.
root_cause: We fixed the bug related to error handling and default settings described above.
solution: Last week on Thursday (4th of August) there was an incident on our backend side that led to configuration values being reverted and some events being processed in a different way for some of our AbuseHQ customers. We reverted the settings to the last backup we had (~20 minutes old).

issue: Production Incident Demand Migration for Teams Affected. We also got confirmation from customers, which were impacted by the API outage, that the provisioning of Microsoft Teams was completed successfully.
root_cause: Our cloud service provider started to roll out the fix and informed us that the fix has already saturated 95% of the tenants.
solution: They are backporting a fix to resolve the issue and anticipate that the problem will be resolved by Wednesday.

issue: SMS Outage - South Africa.
root_cause: We are currently experiencing MT and MO issues to most networks due to an upstream connectivity outage. Engineers are en route to site to investigate.
solution: Upstream has been restored to most networks, currently only MT to Vodacom is still affected by this.

issue: IOS "Pause time" calculation issue.
root_cause: The root cause of the issue is resolved within the latest version (5.21.24) of the Repsly mobile application.
solution: We have resolved the issue in the latest version of the application and will ask users to update to this version (5.21.24).

issue: USSUP-161 Email2sms Outage.
root_cause: Cause: Email2sms services stopped processing traffic due to an issue with IMAP4 authentication.
solution: This issue was escalated to Microsoft who later confirmed that they had disabled IMAP4 on our office365 tenant in advance of the confirmed scheduled switch off October 1st. Microsoft 365 Support responded stating that they had temporarily disabled IMAP4 authentication ahead of its depreciation and had then re-enabled the IMAP4 authentication for our tenant.

issue: This incident occurred in August but was left out of the August report because it did not result in a widespread outage.
root_cause: Several GitHub Actions customers experienced issues because of the degradation so we decided to include it retroactively. there was a sudden spike in traffic to GitHub Actions which resulted in a higher than usual write load on our services.
solution: We mitigated the issue by scaling up the impacted database while also allowing a higher number of concurrent connections to it.

issue: Issue with upstream provider affecting custom domains.
root_cause: Customers with custom domains are experiencing service outages due to an issue with an upstream provider.
solution: We are no longer seeing issues with custom domains and the upstream provider believes the problem has been completely mitigated. We'll continue to post updates while we monitor the situation and confirm when our provider has fully resolved the issue.

issue: Test runner slowdown - Chrome queue. Any customers having received a warning of "10 minute timeout" are encouraged to re-execute the test and contact support if any issues remain.
root_cause: Immediate steps were taken to restore capacity however it was not identified that the code change was causing an ongoing problem until approximately 10pm and test runner capacity gradually diminished over time throughout the day as browser processes ran beyond the 10-minute test run limit due to high resource consumption.
solution: Once the team realized capacity was diminishing again we identified the recent code change as the culprit and immediately rolled back the code.

issue: Cluster node unavailability. This lack of capacity in our cluster led to increased error rates/failed requests, with some end users not being able to view learning activities in FeedbackFruits.
root_cause: Due to the nature of the underlying issue, we monitored our clusters more intensively for the next hours, to be able to prevent reoccurence while the root issue was being resolved by our cloud vendor.
solution: The faulty security update has since been corrected.

issue: Call queue to live chat (SMS deflection) outage.
root_cause: This incident was caused by one of our downstream providers making an undocumented change to their TLS configuration which prevented our telephony platform from triggering the SMS to be sent.
solution: The issue has been fully resolved and a fail-safe implemented to prevent recurrence in the future.

issue: ClassLink SSO Unavailable.
root_cause: Following a production release on the evening of August 8th, our application team found that single sign-on for Classlink rostered users was not functioning as expected, preventing these users from logging in to ThinkLink.
solution: Classlink SSO access has now been restored for all users. Our staging server has been patched and the hotfix is working as expected.

issue: Messages Inappropriate Image Incident.
root_cause: The attack was a result of a coordinated attempt to guess individual user account passwords, sometimes known as a 'credential stuffing' attack.
solution: We completely disabled messaging, blocked the attacker, made sure the image was removed and no longer accessible, and proactively alerted impacted users as well as our wider community. Seesaw’s swift response to this attack included the following steps: - As we resolved the issue, we completely disabled our messaging feature to ensure no one else saw the inappropriate message.

issue: NFTX subgraph syncing issues.
root_cause: This is resulting in a number of subgraphs that use trace to fail at the same block. We have tried to switch our indexer from Erigon to GETH to fix the issue, however GETH does not support trace so the subgraph still fails.
solution: In the meantime we have reverted requests for the holdings to fallback to Web3 calls.

issue: Slido application does not load.
root_cause: The root cause of the issue was the mismatch in the root DNS records for one of the domains we use to provide the service.
solution: There are still problems that we have not been able to fully resolve - mainly connected with the login into the accounts, because of this, we are currently unable to provide a reliable ETA for when full functionality will be restored.

issue: Outage on Invidious and Wiki.
root_cause: This was caused by a change in the way how we handle our database images. We changed to use the most used version of our database in order to delete all mixed different database versions in order to save disk space.
solution: Turns out that Wiki and Invidious didn't like that the database was switched to a older version, so we rolled back the changes for Wiki and Invidious.

issue: Twingate controller service impacted. Medium/Long-term Based on data collected in this incident, we have identified areas where we can improve the behavior of our client and connection applications to better handle similar situations and allow connectivity even under controller downtime.
root_cause: After detailed investigation, we identified two separate issues in the application layer that interacted with each other. First, a code bug caused the system to re-evaluate the permissions of all our users at the same time, causing a significant load that saturated the system.
solution: Continuing to investigate the issue, with software and data migration rolled back to a known state, we initiated the process to fall over to our standby cluster to fully rule out any infrastructure issues.

issue: Slow down on traffic over 62346.
root_cause: The issue was caused by a large campaign from a customer using 62346 that was requested to be sent out immediately.
solution: Then when the backlog had cleared, the campaign messages were release in a gradual sequence to prevent further disruption.

issue: Frontend Builds Not Completing. From ET on September 21st, 2022 to ET on September 22nd, 2022, Shogun Frontend’s site builder was unavailable.
root_cause: This was due to the underlying service that powers the site builder being unavailable for the duration of this incident.
solution: In parallel, Shogun’s Engineering team evaluated and planned alternative solutions if access was not restored in a timely fashion.

issue: Major Service Outage. While looking into the increased error rate, we noticed SSL handshake errors between the caching layer and the workers forwarding requests to origins.
root_cause: Additional debugging surfaced that the SSL handshake failures were caused by the graphcdn.app domain expiring.
solution: We opened an issue on our status page, - We deployed the fix that moved the CDN workers to a different domain and restored service for all requests sent.stellate.sh subdomains or custom domains. Restored access to the graphcdn.app domain, which resolved the issue for any services using graphcdn.app (The time those services were available again varied slightly depending on DNS propagation.) - Marked the incident resolved.

issue: We received an internal report stating that port forwarding was not working on the Codespaces web client and began investigating.
root_cause: We statused yellow due to the broad user impact we were observing. Upon investigation, we found that we missed a step in the secret rotation checklist a few hours earlier, which caused some downstream components to fail to pick up the new secret.
solution: This moment, we considered the incident to be mitigated. Our understanding was that the system would pick up the new secret without intervention, but in reality this secret was picked up only if the process was restarted.

issue: Bolt Sandbox environments are unavailable.
root_cause: A code deployment on 29 SEP 2022 had a bug that resulted degraded performance in the Bolt sandbox environment.
solution: After detection this morning we reverted the code and the sandbox environment was fully operational as of.

issue: INC0042351 - Reading my amatis Cloud disruption.
root_cause: The root cause of this outage was due to a software defect on one of our upstream Cloud switches.
solution: The switches were successfully upgraded to a fixed version of software and have remained stable since.

issue: Data Sync is partially down. The feature will also reduce the risk of downtime if one data center goes offline.
root_cause: We realized that a full sync for impacted stores was necessary to recover the misconfiguration. This was a long process so you could experience slower sync than usual during that time.
solution: What we have done to resolve it The code was immediately reverted to bring the system back to normal.

issue: Downstream services that rely on webhooks to receive their events were unable to receive them, which resulted in service degradation.
root_cause: Webhooks experienced a significant backlog of events caused by a high volume of automated user activity causing a rapid series of create and delete operations.
solution: As a mitigation, we disabled the automated accounts that were causing this activity in order to give us time to find a longer term solution for such activity. Once the automated accounts were disabled, it brought the webhook deliveries back to normal and the backlog got mitigated.

issue: Intermittent build timeouts.
root_cause: We identified certain organisations which faced intermittent build failures PT.
solution: We have rolled back since then and issue is resolved now.

issue: College website down. We estimate this outage was around 10-15 minutes of disruption, however it happened at a time period where traffic is significantly lower than peak times.
root_cause: We have received further information from our hosting provider about this outage. > Our NAT service in EU suffered downtime recently due to a network issue in AWS.
solution: The issue was automatically detected and resolved by AWS after a few minutes.

issue: Problems joining rooms in us-east-1.
root_cause: We identified a brief issue with DNS while deploying a call server (sigh, it's always DNS).
solution: We resolved the issue, and we're monitoring platform operations to ensure that everything has returned to normal.

issue: SevenRooms planned maintenance. In order to achieve this, customers will experience a planned maintenance downtime at approximately that is expected to last for 30 minutes.
root_cause: Working hand-in-hand with the Google Cloud engineering team, the root cause was as resulting from faulty infrastructure deep within the Google Cloud managed database layer (not within the SevenRooms platform application itself), causing deadlock and timeouts for incoming file system requests that were routed to faulty zones.
solution: Our maintenance is complete and all functionality has been restored to SevenRooms.

issue: Delayed Email Sync. Below is an explanation of what happened and how we will prevent another such interruption from occurring.
root_cause: The root cause of this incident was a bug in a vendor’s software introduced during scheduled maintenance on 10/18/2022.
solution: 10/20: Email sync functionality is largely restored.

issue: Migrations stuck in Submitted / Slowness and Degradation in Performance. Our Data Centers are currently experiencing a higher than usual congestion which is causing potential performance degradation of customer migrations.
root_cause: We are seeing performance degradation of customer migrations, which are caused by higher than usual data congestion seen in our MigrationWiz Data Centers.
solution: The backlogged queues at the Data centers are currently being cleared and are getting back to normal, post extensive performance improvement steps taken by our engineers.

issue: Teams for Jira not accessible.
root_cause: We immediately started investigating the issue and found a faulty backend commit that introduced an unwanted change in production. We immediately started rolling back to the last known version, which took about 30 minutes until all affected app servers were back on the working version.
solution: After a few minutes, the first restored app server resulted in partially restored functionality, sometimes after a page reload. Over the course of the next 30 minutes all app servers were rolled back to the fixed version.

issue: Guru Analytics experiencing sporadic loading issues.
root_cause: Because of this we do not have an estimated timeframe to share, but will follow up here as soon as we have an update. Guru's Analytics feature is currently experiencing sporadic performance issues for some users where it is not loading as expected.
solution: We have received confirmation from our analytics provider that they have identified and resolved the issue.

issue: This incident, customers experienced high latency in receiving webhook deliveries, starting GitHub Actions workflow runs, and receiving status updates for in-progress runs.
root_cause: GitHub Actions listens to webhooks to trigger workflow runs, and while investigating we found that the run start delays were caused by a backup in the webhooks queue.
solution: We scaled out and accelerated processing of the webhooks queue as a mitigation. the webhooks queue was fully drained and we statused back to green.

issue: Some User-Generated Interviews Incorrectly Flagged as Spam.
root_cause: The StoryCorps Public Support team is in the process of ensuring every impacted user who received an email alert because of this issue, is notified.
solution: We are happy to confirm that the fix implemented yesterday was successful and all impacted interviews were fully restored and made accessible again in the StoryCorps Online Archive. Within the hour, impacted interviews should be restored, no longer flagged as spam, and accessible like normal through archive.storycorps.org.

issue: Some users cannot log into Close. Below is an explanation of what happened and how we will prevent another such interruption from occurring.
root_cause: One day before the downtime, we published a large change to the way we load our app in order to improve the app'sperformance for our customers.
solution: In order to resolve the issue, we reverted both changes to a previous working version, and we also took the following steps to ensure this type of issue won’t occur anymore: We compared file per file of each release in order to understand the bottom of the issue.

issue: Connectivity Issues. All public connectivity to customer workloads were down during this outage.
root_cause: Technicians discovered that our Washington DC datacenter location became unavailable at around on 11/10 last night and quickly resolved the issue. We are still working with our data center provider IBM and the vendor of the firewall to determine a resolution.
solution: It was discovered that one of the edge firewalls at this location became mostly unresponsive, and services were able to be restored over onto the standby unit.

issue: USSUP-245 Support telephone lines are unavailable. Detection: A customer reported to use through alternative channels that they were receiving a busy signal when attempting to contact 2sms via telephone.
root_cause: Our supplier has provided us with the information that numbers were not hitting our suppliers network, this was due to an upstream routing error.
solution: The carrier found that the cause was a routing issue which was corrected.

issue: San Jose Ongoing Packet Drops. Please expect intermittent network downtime for the next few hours.
root_cause: IT has identified that the San Jose site is experiencing packet drops again this morning, and are actively investigating the issue. If you are onsite, we recommend that you use a mobile hotspot connection to your computer for the huddle and any other calls.
solution: Network has returned to normal operation; IT is monitoring for further packet loss. At the end of the replacement period the network will have intermittent downtime as the connection is being brought back online and tested.

issue: Minor degradation to Real User data ingestion.
root_cause: The problem was caused by a storage issue with one of our cloud service providers in a single geographic region.
solution: The issue appears to have started at ET and all systems were fully restored and operational by ET.

issue: Email to ticket processing issue affecting some customers. Cause: Following an issue with the outgoing email service on 23rd November, a very small number of customers experienced an issue with the TLS handshake of Microsoft servers servicing email relay requests at smtp.office365.com.
root_cause: Whilst investigating this issue, our engineers identified that the same issue could be impacting further customers resulting in the status page notification. The impacted customers were experiencing issues with some of their email to ticket processing.
solution: We have a very mature CI/CD pipeline that is able to build and deploy to all of our regions and the hotfix was deployed to all of our regions within approx.

issue: Server outtage. 🙅‍♀️ Fault Once the mentioned code was deployed to our application servers, it slowly increased the used memory of the Redis instance over a period of three weeks.
root_cause: We immediately started investigating the issue and found that our main Redis instance, which handles asynchronous job processing and caching, had run out of available memory, and therefore all calls to Redis were failing.
solution: The review of the code, we failed to notice a missing flag in our Redis queueing code, which removed completed jobs from Redis. After ~20 minutes AWS was able to provision the resized instance, which restored our API availability.

issue: Salesforce Performance Degradation. Salesforce has confirmed that the performance degradation issues have been resolved in all affected instances.
root_cause: The issue was believed to have been triggered by congestion on various Salesforce database nodes.
solution: Salesforce engineers cleared out the job queues and began application tier restarts which have shown improvement, however, there remain some concerns about database response times.

issue: SecurID Service Incident (NA Region). An incident on December 5th, 2022, caused degraded authentication services for a subset of customers hosted in the NA region from –.
root_cause: The issue was caused by a product defect causing increased processing times on one of our backend nodes.
solution: Once the issue was identified, it was remediated by replacing the impacted node with a healthy node.

issue: Eventbrite - Christmas Events Booking Error.
root_cause: Changes to this event Due to a scheduling error, pricing missing and missing attendee questions on the booking form for the events listed above we have to void all tickets for this session since we do not have the details we need about the young people to keep them all safe.
solution: The following email was sent to attendees--- Hello, I'm writing to inform you that Christmas Crafts in The Hub (Ages 12+) & Christmas Crafts in The Hub (Ages 5-12) have been removed from Eventbrite and will need to be re-booked once they are re-added.

issue: Incident Detected - Azure West US 2 Region Connectivity Issues -. Customers may have been unable to connect to their resources and Virtual Machines (VMs) that were deployed onto the affected nodes may have experienced a restart.
root_cause: A network device experienced a fault, resulting in network connectivity loss to downstream Virtual Machines.
solution: They have restored the power to the top-of-rack (ToR) network devices to mitigate the issue. Affected Virtual Machines may have restarted unexpectedly during this incident.

issue: Device targeting incorrectly matching in certain cases.
root_cause: The cause of the issue was ongoing work to improve device targeting ahead of some changes to the Chrome browser. The work involved shipping a codec to handle any line items or creatives using the previous targeting version until they could be converted to the new version.
solution: We will shortly be conducting an analysis to figure out the exact sequence of events and how to prevent similar issues in the future.

issue: Elevated rates of 503 errors for some ad serving requests. We monitor and alert on the presence of 5xx errors (responses such as 500 internal server error, and 503 service unavailable) on all our servers.
root_cause: The deployment engineer assumes that the receipt of the alert was slightly delayed and was due to an ad server running the “faulty” version of the software before the roll back had completed.
solution: The deployment engineer checks the monitoring system and notices that the ad server on ps16 is still not logging any external ad requests, even though it has been rolled back to the previous software version. The automated checks that alert when an ad server is shutdown are disabled overnight, as otherwise they would continue to fire until the ad server was fixed.

issue: Login elements for web connections not available in Consent UI. There is an issue with the v3 Consent UI: login elements which support web connections are currently not available.
root_cause: Root cause was a misconfiguration of login parameters which caused them not to be rendered in the Consent UI.
solution: Issue has been resolved: login fields are available in the consent UI.

issue: Cloudflare incident on | Cloudflare Blog Skip to content Multiple Cloudflare services were unavailable for 37 minutes.
root_cause: A deployment tool bug caused the production environment to reference a staging build version, routing traffic to an unauthorized endpoint returning HTTP 401 errors, cascading failures across Workers KV, Pages, Access, and Turnstile.
solution: What follows is a discussion of what went wrong, how the incident was resolved, and the work we are undertaking to ensure it does not happen again. When access to KV was restored, some Waiting Room users would have experienced queuing as the service came back up.

issue: Service disruption at Turso (see incident report).
root_cause: Incorrectly configured DB backup identifiers led to data leaks for free tier customers, and the subsequent fix resulted in possible data loss.
solution: They are scaled back to one automatically upon receiving a network request.

issue: Heroku sync integrations are failing.
root_cause: Doppler syncs secrets to Heroku via a Heroku OAuth application.
solution: Once the integration is reconnected, Doppler will re-enable all associated syncs that have been disabled and perform a fresh sync.

issue: Service Interruption. To note, although login and signup services were interrupted during the incident, submissions were functioning throughout and no data was lost.
root_cause: The incident was caused by an expired SSL certificate failing to update due to an integration issue with our security supplier.
solution: All services have been restored with logins and signups working as they should. Our engineering teams will review the details and ensure we put measures in place to prevent this from happening again.

issue: Unable to sync secrets, webhooks, and activity log notifications. From 2023-01-16 to 2023-01-16, Doppler experienced a partial outage which prevented sync integrations, webhooks, and activity log notifications from executing.
root_cause: We’ve also identified that the ability for API clients to fetch secrets should not be dependent on our application’s ability to connect to RabbitMQ.
solution: On 2023-01-13, Doppler’s security team rotated a RabbitMQ password, mistakenly identifying the credential as unused in production. The change was deployed and the incident was resolved at 2023-01-16.

issue: Internet Network (NSW) - Intermittent DNS server fault.
root_cause: Some NBN services in NSW may be experiencing intermittent browsing issues due to a suspected DNS server fault.
solution: Service has now been restored to full functionality.

issue: Background updates failing.
root_cause: Due to an upgrade earlier today, background updates started failing. Crates published since have not been added to the index yet but remain in the queue.
solution: We have reverted the change and restarted the workers.

issue: Incoming call issue from Spark: Post mortem update.
root_cause: However, it was determined that this was not freeing up the memory resources on the underlying operating system node.
solution: Previous attempts to resolve the issue only restarted the server process.

issue: Twingate Service Incident. On January 24 our on-call team started to receive automated alerts regarding system performance degradation.
root_cause: This incident occurred because of two independent events that occurred simultaneously that in turn were made worse due to deployed Connectors and Clients with out of date behaviors.
solution: Upgraded our infrastructure provider’s load balancer to improve container-awareness Short Term.

issue: Multiple Microsoft Services are down affecting Workspot Customers. Microsoft reported a global outage for Office 365 & Azure Portal services.
root_cause: Preliminary We determined that a change made to the Microsoft Wide Area Network (WAN) impacted connectivity between clients on the internet to Azure, as well as connectivity between services in different regions, as well as ExpressRoute connections.
solution: Microsoft confirmed that the issues have been mitigated. We identified a recent change to WAN as the underlying cause and have rolled back this change.

issue: Technical Issue with dashboard availability. This forced us to make some changes on the backend to prevent any performance degradation while working without distributed filesystem at all.
root_cause: We opened a case with AWS, as we worked around the clock on a plan to make our system responsive again, without knowing that the root cause had started on Amazon side.
solution: We replaced the file system for another one with more aggressive settings.

issue: Intermittent delays loading Web UI and running searches. This led to slow searches and slow load times for any part of the Web UI that displays data about logs.
root_cause: Upon investigation, we found that it had not shut down cleanly and some files essential to a normal startup had not been written to disk.
solution: Pods were gradually moved to other nodes and restarted, so as to prevent any interruption in service. We made manual edits to the pod that had not restarted cleanly so it could start again.

issue: Issues connecting to calls.
root_cause: We were ultimately able to prove that the deadlocking behavior was caused by a low-level behavior change introduced in a point release of MySQL.
solution: We had upgraded the database server over the weekend, but it had been operating normally since Monday. The alerts indicated a high level of lock contention on the newly upgraded database, which was causing problems for our call servers (SFUs).

issue: Based on learnings from this incident, we are evaluating expanding our regional redundancy and have started making architectural changes to better handle temporary regional and datacenter outages, including more regularly exercising our failover capabilities.
root_cause: On February 7 our monitors detected failures creating, starting, and connecting to GitHub Codespaces in the Southeast Asia region, caused by a datacenter outage of our cloud provider.
solution: Codespaces in that region recovered automatically when the datacenter recovered, allowing existing codespaces in the region to be restarted.

issue: Event app is unreachable in some regions. On Tuesday, Thursday 9th the infrastructure team triggered a capacity upgrade on our caching system in favour of improving the latency and user experience on the current & up-coming events, this action is commonly execute and part of recurrent task.
root_cause: In parallel, the cause of the issue was investigated and mitigations were put in place. Mitigation deployment Traffic disruption stopped as the same time than the cache capacity upgrade were reverted.
solution: Swapcard confirmed that the update was completed and capacity restored to pre-incident levels, ensuring that the traffic was back to the pre-incident rate.

issue: Invalid Role Lockout. Synopsis Customer was unable to login and received "unable to process callback" error.
root_cause: A bug discovered in Teleport 11.3.2 was the result of new validation that prevented login when invalid namespaces were used in role templates.
solution: Teleport Cloud tenant was upgraded to v11.3.2 the previous day. Customer’s tenant was rolled back to 11.2.1, the faulty role was corrected, and the tenant was upgraded again to 11.3.2.

issue: Searches are running slowly. The rate of requests was high enough to slow down all requests related to search results within the pod’s zone (one out of three total).
root_cause: As a side effect of the previous incident, the pod incorrectly determined that data was missing from the local disk and began sending http requests to our S3 storage to locate the missing data.
solution: In a previous incident on (more details at two pods storing logs were temporarily removed from the pool of pods available for receiving and inserting new batches of logs into our data store. We removed the pod from the pool available for receiving and inserting new batches of logs into our data store.

issue: Relay2 (us-east4) and Relay4 (eu-west6) Issue.
root_cause: Further investigation, we determined that an error in our Terraform configuration affecting network firewall rules had caused the issue.
solution: We disabled pods in the two affected clusters, which caused connected Clients and Connectors to re-connect to the next closest Relay cluster. At we corrected the error and redeployed the affected clusters, which resolved the issue.

issue: Blank page or buggy styling issue.
root_cause: We've identified the issue, and it's caused by a corrupted cached file on our CDN. So this no longer affects new users loading Kami, but any affected users should still clear their full browser cache (including both "Cached images and files" and "Cookies and other site data"), restart their browser and then load Kami again.
solution: We have reports of users who tried these steps which resolved the issue We're sorry for the inconvenience.

issue: Campus Power Issues. For buildings that do not have power or generator backup power, the WiFi and network is also unavailable in that building.
root_cause: Consumers energy is estimating that power will be restored to most campus buildings by February 24th at 10am but due to the scope of the outages this time may change.
solution: Consumers energy shows two outages for the SAU apartments, and one is estimated to be restored on February 23 (today) and the other shows February 25th.

issue: Inbound SMS Outage to 27600 Number ranges.
root_cause: The outage was caused by a data centre power issue that caused a uncontrolled server shut down. This then resulted in our upstream's SMSC services not booting.
solution: The boot issue was resolved when the vendor fixed the clustering service. Our provider has restored the primary SMSC after engaging with their Vendor.

issue: Doppler CLI Failing to Install Due to GitHub Incident. This resulted in disruptions to their workflows and GitHub actions relying on the Doppler CLI.
root_cause: This issue was due to a related incident on GitHub, where Doppler hosts all CLI binaries and signatures. According to GitHub's incident report, GitHub experienced degraded performance and increased error rates for their packages service.
solution: GitHub resolved the incident after a few hours, and users were once again able to install the Doppler CLI.

issue: Users are unable to start sessions when using older versions of Frame Enterprise Profile Driver.
root_cause: This is due to an expired driver certificate. The solution is to update the Frame Enterprise Profile Driver to version 6.8.4.8008 using our Frame Agent Setup Tool ( on the Sandbox and run a Publish on affected Accounts.
solution: All instances already on must be rebooted for the update to take effect.

issue: Unable to load data in Jira Cloud.
root_cause: Test disabling browser cache to see if it fixes a problem ( If issues still occur after following those two steps, please report the issue at as the issue is caused by a separate problem.
solution: Users can follow the steps in these videos to help determine if remaining problems are due to cache that still needs to be cleared or if there is a separate problem to report: 1. We disabled our server cache, re-deployed code, then re-enabled our server cache.

issue: All MySQL servers on this problematic node experienced connection delays and slow query execution, leading to the high failure rate.
root_cause: We determined the root cause to be an unhealthy disk on a VM node hosting our database, which caused significant performance degradation at the OS level.
solution: We mitigated this with a failover of the database.

issue: Spark Calling Issues. Spark are working with upstream carrier to reset SS7 links which are in a 'timeout' state due to earlier issues.
root_cause: The Spark issues are ongoing due to a resource issue at Spark to work on the fault. We have started to reroute calls via an alternate path and have already moved a couple hundred high volume/priority numbers to get them back in service.
solution: Upstream carrier advises that their systems are restored and they expect to have their SBCs operational again shortly. No specific ETA on this but they are prioritising the SBC system restoration and expect service to be restored shortly.

issue: Web App Outage - Permission issues on Kube cluster. We are currently experiencing an outage that is affecting our web app.
root_cause: It appears to be caused by a permission issue in our Kubernetes cluster.
solution: We have deployed a fix and are monitoring the issue.

issue: Inbound SMS Outage to 27600 Number ranges.
root_cause: Technicians were able to reduce DC temperatures caused by the AC issue. Vendor has confirmed this is being caused by an AC failure in the DC.
solution: Updates to follow Our vendor has confirmed this was due to power fluctuations within the DC and have restored the SMSC. We are working with our vendor to get the service restored ASAP.

issue: S2 - O365 calendar Errors - 401/The parameter count cannot be less than zero errors.
root_cause: In efforts to resolve this issue, our team found the root cause to be related to a hotfix that was released on the evening of Monday.
solution: The hot fix was released to resolve an auto refresh issue that involved calendar credentials, thus causing 401 unauthorized errors. We are currently investigating an issue with O365 Calendar Errors - Customers are receiving emails about their calendar sync being disabled.

issue: Next Advantage Hosted Voice & SIP Outage. We are starting to see services slowly restore.
root_cause: The upstream carrier has acknowledged there is a major outage and are currently investigating. Call issues are now also affecting inbound calls.
solution: The majority of our customers services have restored. We do now have access to divert calls if your services have not restored.

issue: On March 15 our monitors detected increased latency for requests to Container, NPM, Nuget, RubyGems package registries.
root_cause: This was caused by an operation on the primary database host that was performed as part of routine maintenance.
solution: The maintenance, a slow running query that was not properly drained blocked all database resources. We remediated this issue by killing the slow running query and restarting the database.

issue: Functional Outage: On Demand Migration OneDrive. Customers may have to wait two hours before the API will return updated values after customers move their domain from the source to the target tenant.
root_cause: Our Cloud Service Provider started to roll out a fix to resolve the service degradation.
solution: Our Cloud Service Provider has deployed a fix and we can confirm that the issue has been resolved for impacted customers. Our Cloud Service Provider also informed us that it could take up to 24 hours until the fix has been applied to all tenants globally.

issue: Intermittent 404s downloading Node.js.
root_cause: The origin server for nodejs.org was being overloaded, and due to a recent configuration change, was now erroneously returning 404 responses for valid files when it was overloaded and couldn't read them from its disk.
solution: The Incident Starting on March 15th and going through to March 17th (with much of the issue being mitigated on the 16th), users were receiving intermittent 404 responses when trying to download Node.js from nodejs.org, or even accessing parts of the website. A build script bug caused by the recent migration of the website to Next.js resulted in the site being rebuilt and the entire Cloudflare cache being purged every five minutes, sending an abnormally high number of requests to the origin server and putting it under excessive load.

issue: Issue with upstream provider delaying certain tasks.
root_cause: Our upstream provider has resolved the incident. Today's Metrics are updating normally and all scheduled Posts are delivering as expected.
solution: They'll be updated and delivered as soon as the problem has been fixed. We'll continue to post updates while we monitor the situation and confirm when our provider has fully resolved the issue.

issue: Capsule is unavailable or slow. We're very sorry if you suffered from the periods of slow responses and elevated error rates with Capsule yesterday.
root_cause: We’ve tracked the issue down the a bug in our data stores query optimiser that resulted in what should have been a fast responding query taking several minutes to complete.
solution: While we fully understand the exact nature of the optimiser bug we have applied a fix that stops the bug from occurring.

issue: On March 27 users began to see degraded experience with Git Operations, GitHub Issues, pull requests, GitHub Actions, GitHub API requests, GitHub Codespaces, and GitHub Pages.
root_cause: The cause was traced to a change in a frequently-used database query. The query alteration was part of a larger infrastructure change that had been rolled out gradually, starting in October 2022, then more quickly beginning February 2023, completing.
solution: The query causing lock tension was disabled via feature flag, and then refactored. We have added additional monitoring of relevant database resources so as not to reach resource exhaustion, and detect similar issues earlier in our staged rollout process.

issue: On March 29 users began to see a degraded experience with GitHub Actions with their workflows not progressing.
root_cause: We determined the cause of the impact to be a degraded database cluster. Contributing factors included a new load source from a background job querying that database cluster, maxed out database transaction pools, and underprovisioning of vtgate proxy instances that are responsible for query routing, load balancing, and sharding.
solution: The incident was mitigated through throttling of job processing and adding capacity, including overprovisioning to speed processing of the backlogged jobs.

issue: Event app increase response time. On March 29th, 2023 the infrastructure team triggered a capacity upgrade on our main API in favor of improving the latency and user experience on the current & up-coming events.
root_cause: In parallel, the cause of the issue was investigated and mitigations were put in place. Mitigation deployment Latency dropped as the same time than the capacity upgrade on our main gateway was triggered.
solution: Swapcard confirmed that the scaling was completed and latency restored to pre-incident levels, ensuring that the traffic was back to the pre-incident rate.

issue: Connectivity Issues. This “large scale regional event” caused traffic from us-west-2 to move from Oregon Edge (HOI) to Seattle Edge locations (SEA4 and SEA19), which triggered AnyCast shifts between the two Seattle Edge locations resulting in connection timeouts for traffic originating from us-west-2.
root_cause: The root cause of this incident was a routing misconfiguration by AWS.
solution: This configuration change proved unsuccessful and the configurations were reverted.

issue: Elevated 500 errors on Read Event.
root_cause: This was due to a bug released at this time which allowed a small number of events to cause an error while being rendered.
solution: This was immediately spotted and rolled back, which was completed.

issue: Box responses are randomly slower. Date 2023-03-31 Authors Lukas Danek, CPO Michael Zabka, CTO Michal Artazov, DevOps Lead On the 31st of March 2023, our production cluster experienced an issue where box responses were randomly slower than expected.
root_cause: This report aims to provide a detailed analysis of the impact, trigger, detection, root causes, and the steps taken for remediation. The slowdown in box responses had a negative impact on the user experience.
solution: This strategy ensures that outdated data is promptly removed from the cache, reducing the chances of serving stale responses.

issue: Some networks currently unreachable. Our engineers have attempted to route traffic away from the Auckland-IX peering Exchange to resolve the connectivity problems until the outage on AKL-IX has been resolved.
root_cause: Impacts were seen between peers on pe2.akl3 at MDR and pe3.akl1 at Datacentre220 with the root cause still under analysis. Our engineers have confirmed that the AKL-IX peering is now fixed and we are able to connect with those peers previously affected by this outage on AKL-IX so we will begin moving traffic back to the AKL-IX peering exchange shortly and we are marking this event as resolved.
solution: We will set the status to resolved once AKL-IX have resolved the problem on their network and traffic has been re-established with AKL-IX.

issue: Increased delays on Jira Cloud and Jira Service Management Cloud integrations while creating/updating Opsgenie alerts in US region. The Incident caused degradation to customers hosted in the US region only.
root_cause: The issue was caused by the sudden spike in the volume of messages, due to bulk actions.
solution: The incident was mitigated by scaling the integration component, which put Atlassian systems into a known good state.

issue: Partial outage. This patch caused some of the Redis instances in our system to fail, making the reservation service unavailable.
root_cause: After investigating this issue, it was discovered that the root cause was a security patch that was applied to Redis by AWS.
solution: This issue was resolved which resulted in a total downtime of 10 minutes. Shortly after the login issue was resolved, users reported that they could not access the system's reservation module.

issue: Delays in Android push notifications. REMEDIAL ACTIONS PLAN & NEXT STEPS We know that outages impact your productivity.
root_cause: The issue was caused by an incident in a third party messaging service, which is responsible for delivering push notifications to Android devices.
solution: The overall impact was - in Opsgenie_._ The incident only resulted in delays in Android push notifications only, and these notifications were delivered successfully after FCM service was restored and no data loss occurred.

issue: Data processing delay, April 6th.
root_cause: The root cause of the issue has been determined and has been resolved. Some users may still experience slight delays in the data processing.
solution: Kindly note that the data sync issue has been resolved as the data processing is now under control.

issue: US API degradation. This resulted in no further alarms to alert us to the degradation of the service, and reinforced the belief that the service was healthy again.
root_cause: This time, our monitoring system was not alerting, as the although the metric for measuring HTTP 500 was reporting correctly, the alarm was misconfigured.
solution: The secondary node was promoted and the cluster failed over automatically, recovering as planned. When a failover occurs, the original failed node is rebooted, and then becomes the read-only partner in the cluster, whilst the existing read-only secondary node is promoted to primary.

issue: Functional outage for Public Folders. Therefore the service disruptions in some tenants may still be present until the fix has been globally applied to all tenants.
root_cause: Quest will contact our Cloud Service Provider for a root cause analysis that can be shared later with customers.
solution: However we can confirm that the issue has been resolved for most of our impacted customers. Our Cloud Service Provider is still deploying the fix, and we can confirm that the issue has been resolved for some impacted customers.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption in North American Region – Web User Interface. at approximately Pacific, some customers reported an issue to xMatters Customer Support where users were encountering errors when attempting to log in to the xMatters web interface.
root_cause: The issue was caused when a customer inadvertently initiated a denial-of-service attack by launching an excessive number of API requests.
solution: Once the traffic was mitigated, impacted systems were able to recover and customers were migrated back to their original data centers.

issue: Sites running on MySQL 20 are inaccessible.
root_cause: At MST, we identified customers on MySQL 20 were receiving the error message "Unable to connect to any of the specified MySQL hosts" when connecting to their ECP site.
solution: We started investigating this as soon as we received alerts and rebooted the server to address the issue. We identified the issue then corrected it after which performance returned to normal for that server.

issue: The impact resulted in an 11 minute outage of access to issues and pull request related artifacts.
root_cause: The root cause of this incident was a planned change in our database infrastructure to minimize the impact of unsuccessful deployments.
solution: The incident was resolved when traffic automatically switched back to the existing nodes.

issue: Platform Incident - Ingestion Outage. We are currently experiencing an outage on our content ingestion systems.
root_cause: We've identified the fault and are currently in the process of restoring our ingestion platform. Once the ingestion platform is functional again we can begin ingesting pending deliveries and will provide a further update at that time.
solution: The backlog will be cleared gradually as we ramp up processing capacity.

issue: The Web UI is not accessible. This made the Mongo database unavailable to other services.
root_cause: The WebUI relies entirely on Mongo for account information and therefore became unresponsive, returning an error of “failure to get a peer from the ring-balancer.” While the immediate reason for the incident is clear, the root cause is still unknown.
solution: We removed the WebUI from the service mesh.

issue: Analytics API is unreachable and data ingestion delayed, analytics may falsely appear empty. Affected customers may have been impacted by varying degrees and with a shorter timescale, this.
root_cause: In parallel, the cause of the issue was investigated and mitigations were put in place. Mitigation deployment In favour of restoring the Analytics services, our first mitigation has been too attempt an hard restart of the database, has documented in our response plan, to free stacking queries (force query termination), we notice that the restart were not providing the expected effect and the queries were still stacking and not getting resolved.
solution: Once the indexes were restored to their proper state, the Analytics API has been switch back to the normal database and pipeline has been restored to ensure analytics metrics were properly computed and delivered. Swapcard confirmed that the restoration was completed and API & underline features restored.

issue: Events and Actions Outage in US East PoP. Events are not Being Dispatched.
root_cause: Impact, and Resolution On Tuesday we observed that Events and Actions messages were not being processed on our US PoP or EU Central PoP.
solution: Shortly after observing the issue, we redeployed a processing schema, and the issue was resolved.

issue: WebMobile Service unavailable. During the incident, web and mobile users could not log in to the Repsly web portal or Repsly mobile application, and all users who were logged in to the mobile application could not synchronize data.
root_cause: Service was unavailable between - because of a problem with our servers.
solution: After we resolved the issue, all data was synced, and there was no data loss.

issue: Some clusters failing to restart following Tenant Upgrade. Their service was disrupted for up to 2.5 hours.
root_cause: It was determined that a change to the Okta access request code was leading to a panic.
solution: To prevent any other tenants from impact (upon creation of an access request) the balance of tenants were also downgraded to the previous version (v12.2.4).

issue: Google Safe Browsing flag as malware.
root_cause: In our investigation we’ve identified that the same library is also available from GitHub and many Linux and BSD distro packages.
solution: Google Safe Browsing has removed the malware flag from rubygems.org.

issue: Media capabilities degraded. The service disruption lasted for one hour and 32 minutes, and caused service disruption to customers with services hosted in the us-west-1 region.
root_cause: The issue was caused by an attempted migration of a service to a new network segment.
solution: The incident was detected within three minutes by automated monitoring and mitigated by a rollback of the change which put Atlassian systems into a known good state. As part of this migration, a DNS record pointing to the old network segment was not updated, which resulted in failure when the old network stack was removed.

issue: Event App & Studio are unresponsive. We would like to provide you with a post-mortem report concerning a service delivery disruption that impacted Swapcard customers on Wednesday, the 17th of May, 2023.
root_cause: This issue arose due to a recent upgrade of the pods scheduler version, combined with a specific parameter that caused problems in a particular scenario.
solution: Swapcard officially confirmed that services had been restored to pre-incident levels, ensuring that traffic had returned to its previous rate before the incident: The majority of services were restored, and additional mitigation measures were implemented.

issue: Consent Engagements not Showing. Overview Between ET and ET Admiral experienced an outage with European Consent, which resulted in the failure to convey or prompt for consent for users subject to GDPR.
root_cause: The root cause of this outage was identified as a misconfiguration in a file, the Global Vendor List (GVL), provided by the Interactive Advertising Bureau (IAB).
solution: Steps To address the misconfiguration issue and mitigate the impact of the outage, Admiral has temporarily suspended the periodic, automatic, updates of the GVL.

issue: Popup and embedded secure payload failures.

solution: However, we have resolved the issue and all transactions have been processed successfully.

issue: Telecommunication Services Internet Outage (Hillsborough, NJ Infrastructure). Issue The cause was an internet outage from our main ISP backhaul Comcast in the area of our Hillsborough Township, NJ infrastructure for required service maintenance.
root_cause: Our failover ISP did not come online automatically and system engineers begin investigating, engineers found a misconfiguration with our main routing switch.

To prevent this from happening again, we will.

issue: Problems accessing Healthtrack.

solution: Our systems switched to backup after a brief interruption, and service was restored automatically within a few minutes.

issue: Outage on Vivantio for a small number of customers. issue: Events Webapp Outage. The Events Webapp outage has been fully resolved.

root_cause: The team diligently investigated the root cause of the incidents, considering that slow Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks are typically challenging to detect due to their integration with legitimate traffic.

issue: Intermittent latency on the event app & studio causing error page or latency. We would like to provide you with a post-mortem report concerning a service delivery disruption that impacted Swapcard customers on Thursday, the 15th of June, 2023.
root_cause: This issue arose due to an undetected memory leak, which resulted in intensive garbage collection tasks. As a consequence, memory was not freed up properly, and the CPU usage became significantly high.
solution: Mitigation deployment To resolve the issue, our initial course of action involved implementing a mitigation strategy that gradually scaled up the various services: The incident was successfully mitigated, and the system regained its pre-incident capacity.

issue: Increased error rate in Sandbox.

issue: Dégradation de Performance / Performance Degradation. EN/ Issue Summary On June 26th 2023, a performance degradation was experienced by some users of the platform, affecting the display time of product pages.
root_cause: An update of our distributed cache system was made, which caused an overconsumption of memory in our applications: this overconsumption then caused latency at the interface level.
solution: We have rolled back the technical component to its previous version.

issue: Delay on messaging, notifications and simulated live stream processing. On Tuesday, June 28th the Incident Response team identified the issue related to the internal messaging system, a message queue was full and disrupting performance for the other queues present in the same system.
root_cause: In parallel, the cause of the issue is being investigated and mitigations were put in place. Mitigation deployment To ensure proper processing of all messages, the service responsible for handling these messages has been scaled-up to process more messages than nominal levels to compensate for the buildup.
solution: On Tuesday, June 28th the Incident Response team resolved the incident. Swapcard confirmed that the incident was resolved and delay restored to pre-incident levels, ensuring that the processing speed was back to the pre-incident rate.

issue: Partial service failure due to non-volatile Redis saturation. However, the utilization of our non-volatile Redis, which usually hovers below 5%, slowly started to increase.
root_cause: Earlier today, we deployed a bug that exposed a legacy system to excessive traffic, overwhelming our core Redis instance and causing cascading failures in certain functionality.
solution: Engineering quickly identified the issue and cleared excess data from Redis, restoring service. May 29th, - Fix deployed to remove the tracking bug We deployed a fix to remove the tracking bug.

issue: June 25th, 2023 Deno Deploy Postmortem. Learn more -> Dismiss June 25th, 2023 Deno Deploy Postmortem Heyang Zhou Luca Casonato Satya Rohith Bert Belder Deno Deploy On June 25th, 2023, at a large chunk of Deno Deploy services experienced a service disruption until approximately (44 minutes).
root_cause: On Sunday, June 25, a DDOS attack was mounted against one of the web properties hosted on Deno Deploy.
solution: Unfortunately our database was unable to handle the query load associated with this, which resulted in some nodes coming online much slower than expected, while others would time out while waiting for their start-up payload and subsequently rebooted themselves, which exacerbated the load on our database further.

issue: Performance issues and outages with Cloud products. One specific issue, which turned out to be a red herring, related to the functionality to forward core API requests to the Edge API.

issue: Twingate Service Incident -. issue: Error on login. As a result, the database cluster became unavailable, affecting our services and user logins.

issue: Increased background job latency in APAC region. On August 25th, FeedbackFruits experienced an incident that caused an increased latency in background job processing.
root_cause: This was able to resolve the delay and allow our engineers to start investigating the root cause and apply a fix. Cause of the issue The issues were caused by a oversight in the logic that is responsible for ensuring the progress calculation happens efficiently, which caused progress to continuously be recalculated, resulting in a buildup of background jobs and corresponding delays.
solution: After becoming aware of the problem, an engineer noticed the scaling was not working correctly and manually scaled up the capacity of our background processing to attempt to deal with the backlog of jobs waiting to be processed.

issue: Web UI is unresponsive and ingestion of log lines halted. The Web UI did not load and log lines could not be sent by either our agent or API.
root_cause: The pods running our Kong Gateway were overwhelmed with connection requests. CPU increased to a point that health checks started to fail and the pods were shut down.
solution: We manually scaled up the number of pods devoted to running our Kong Gateway.

issue: Files Uploading is not working.

issue: Multiple product logins. SUMMARY some customers were unable to login to Atlassian's Cloud products using id.atlassian.com.

solution: Users with existing sessions were not impacted, traffic was incrementally restored to a previous build, mitigating the impact for users. We are prioritizing the following improvement actions to avoid repeating this type of incident: Automated tests to be put in place to validate that cookies are not being removed from responses.

issue: Timeouts and High Latencies Across All Regions.
root_cause: The problem arose as a result of a Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack targeting the Ably default endpoint, which temporarily overloaded various elements of Ably's networking and request handling infrastructure.
solution: When there is an abnormally severe load spike, there can be a period of time in which the cluster in a region is under-provisioned, which results in some fraction of requests being denied until the required capacity is in place.

issue: Increased Latency and Reduced Availability in the US, EU, and Global Region Groups. Between January 9th and January 13th, users in our US, EU, and Global Region Groups experienced multiple periods of increased latency and reduced availability.
root_cause: The issue was caused by a series of DDoS attacks that were targeted at a set of our customers, resulting in extreme waves of traffic to Fauna, each of which were many orders of magnitude above our baseline traffic patterns.
solution: After initial investigation, engineers realized that despite the fact that the requests were being throttled and sent a 429 response at the compute layer due to exceeding throughput limits, routing nodes were still experiencing resource starvation due to the number of connections being held and resources associated with request handling being kept in memory. Engineers identified and blocked offending accounts, causing the compute layer to short circuit the normal request handling process and return 410 responses for requests from those accounts, which shortened the time that each connection wa.

issue: PyPI Simple Index Timing Out. PyPI experienced an outage which resulted in serving 500-level responses for certain requests, including requests to a subset of the Simple Repository API.
root_cause: While the actual details of this new functionality is unrelated, a misconfiguration of this new service resulted in views that depended on this service failing to successfully serve a response, which was missed by PyPI’s unit test suite and by manual testing of the feature branch.
solution: As a result of PyPI’s container orchestration and deployment service not explicitly supporting rollbacks, issues like this are generally resolved by introducing a new pull request which reverts the problematic commit, which in turn is merged and deployed. This migration could not be reverted simply by reverting the commit, as deployment would fail when it would attempt to bring the database up to date with the migration history, and find that the current migration version was no longer present.

issue: Platform instability. On PT, Hex customers experienced platform instability, including issues with kernel execution and site access.
