solution: Once the database stabilized, we rolled back the migration change, fully restoring service by PT.

issue: YugabyteDB Aeon cluster edits are failing.
root_cause: We identified an issue with editing existing clusters in YugabyteDB Aeon, which is failing in certain scenarios.
solution: The issue has been mitigated, and a maintenance patch including an OS upgrade is available as a maintenance event. The Yugabyte team will monitor the progress, and once the maintenance event is complete, cluster edit operations will be re-enabled.

issue: Partial data capture issues (web & mobile). Postmortem 2024/11/13 Failed Tasks Not Retried / Pages Not Initialized On October 31st, 2024, an issue introduced in our service caused a small percentage (< 0.05%) of sessions to not process a portion of data within them.
root_cause: Due to a code change that altered the behavior of an uncommon failure condition, part of our system marked the data in question to be “completed” when it had actually failed.
solution: After noticing some odd system behavior and finding that we had unprocessed data that should have been successful, we quickly traced it back to the code change, and deployed a fix immediately that would ensure no future data gets into this state.

issue: Partial API Performance Degradation.
root_cause: A database cloud provider is experiencing unusually high load which is causing degraded performance on certain pages and API endpoints.
solution: The provider has implemented a fix which appears to have restored performance levels, we're monitoring the situation to assure stability now.

issue: Degraded performance in the EU-West-2 (Paris) region. On Sunday 17 November at an incident occurred in the eu-central-2 (Paris) region, resulting in elevated HTTP 5XX error responses and slow response times to buckets impacting some customers.
root_cause: An upgrade to the region, an error caused the service to allocate more connections than needed resulting in an overload to one of the service components.
solution: To address the situation, the Operations Team reverted the update to restore service. The error was corrected and the update was subsequently re-deployed successfully.

issue: Data Centre Outage. A power outage in the Netherlands, where out data centre is based, has led to a complete outage affecting 28,000 residents and international users relying on the data centre based there.
root_cause: We believe this issue has been worsened due to failure of the backup generators.
solution: We are hoping the service is restored shortly.

issue: Elevated errors after deployment.
root_cause: We've deployed an update that caused elevated errors due to a caching error that didn't surface during testing.
solution: We've rolled back the update, implemented a fix, and rolled out the fixed update.

issue: The notifications service was degraded and stopped sending notifications to all our dotcom customers.
root_cause: This was due to a database host coming out of a regular maintenance process in read-only mode.
solution: We mitigated the incident by making the host writable again. To prevent similar incidents moving forward, we are working to improve our observability across database clusters to reduce our time to detection and improve our system resilience on startup.

issue: Portals with EU domain name down.
root_cause: This delay occurs due to the DNS propagation process, during which DNS information is updated across the internet.
solution: Our team has taken corrective actions, and the service is now in the process of being restored.

issue: Callbridge Conferencing - Delayed Service Response. After a couple of weeks of random interruptions to the Google Calendar add- it reached a point where the concurrent requests to change existing meeting schedules are causing database deadlock and transaction rollbacks.
root_cause: Summary of Root Cause Google Workspace made some internal changes at around the beginning of November 2024, which changes the Google Calendar add-on behavior. We have observed that the add-on would resubmit the same meeting changes to our platform during event synchronization and caused a large increase in the number of API requests.
solution: Action Plan to Prevent Future Service Incidents We have disabled all Google Calendar add-ons on 11/25 We will rewrite how we process the Google Calendar updates so that all changes to a given account are serialized (instead of updating meetings in parallel) We will collect logs to open a ticket with Google Workspace team to understand their changes We scaled up the system to increase capacity, meanwhile Google Workspace paused the requests to us.

issue: Callbridge Conferencing - Delayed Service Response.
root_cause: We identified an issue caused by the Google Calendar add- which impacted the performance of our video conferencing platform.
solution: To resolve this issue, we have temporarily disabled some Google Calendar integration features. We will follow up with an email once the service has been restored.

issue: Increased Errors across Affirm Services. Affirm is still experiencing degraded service and high error rates.
root_cause: The root cause is related to excessive traffic on our backend database.
solution: The issue has been resolved and all services have been restored to full functionality.

issue: Order Fulfillment - Issue Detected.
root_cause: The incident was caused by a bad deployment of new set of rules in one of the critical internal services.
solution: The incident was quickly mitigated by reverting the change. To prevent this in future we have introduced more checks and process when making changes in critical flows.

issue: Microsoft 365 Service Degradation. We have been made aware of a possible Service Degradation on the Microsoft platform in EMEA and globally.
root_cause: Microsoft Status We have received a further update from Microsoft Microsoft Status We've isolated the root cause and have developed a patch, which we're testing on a subset of components before full deployment.
solution: We have received an update from Microsoft confirming that services have been fully restored.

issue: Unavailability of uploading from 3rd Party Services. Incident Summary the “Uploading from 3rd Party Services” feature of our platform was unavailable.
root_cause: The outage was caused by a synchronization issue between repositories during a server configuration update.
solution: The incident was fully resolved, and service was restored. The application configuration was updated and service functionality was fully restored.

issue: Hasura Cloud AWS us-east-1: Increased error rates and latency. This surge caused elevated latency and error rates across projects in the region, with some projects experiencing up to 90% dropped traffic during peak periods.
root_cause: Third Spike ( - PT) 12.41M requests Peak of 30,000 requests/second at approximately Root Cause Our gateway clusters, which are shared across all projects in a region, were unable to scale quickly enough to handle the sudden flood of requests.
solution: Preventive Measures We are implementing the following improvements to prevent similar incidents.

issue: Elevated URL API Errors. On 26 November 2024, an issue with our URL API was identified, causing a partial outage of the service.
root_cause: The issue was caused by a CDN configuration change that altered cache key behavior, significantly increasing traffic to our origin servers.
solution: The incident was fully resolved, and service was restored. The configuration change was identified as the root cause and rolled back.

issue: Fiber to Premise Outage - Bard, Griswold and Hall Road areas. Customers with FTTx service near the Bard, Griswold, and Hall Road area near Cassadaga may be experiencing a service outage.
root_cause: Service has been restored - Network Operations and DFT Outside Plant teams will continue to monitor Due to a motor vehicle accident, DFT’s Fiber Optic Equipment was severely damaged.
solution: All services have been restored, and DFT technicians are now cleared from the site.

issue: VSE Issue under investigation. Incident Report Incident Start Date: 01/12/2024 Incident End Date: 01/12/2024 Summary On the evening of December 1st, our monitoring systems detected degraded performance in our Virtual Staging Environment.
root_cause: The disruption was triggered by an unexpected surge in traffic to our Virtual Staging Environment.
solution: To resolve the issue, we promptly scaled up the service to handle the increased load.

issue: Slow Page Loading and Intermittent Login Issues. On Monday December 2, Incident IQ experienced a service interruption that caused degradation of services for several customers.
root_cause: Services were ultimately restored by a combination of manually adding infrastructure resources and the automated scaling job completion Incident IQ is working alongside Microsoft and have identified that unforeseeable abnormally high transactions on the SQL environment during scaling caused the process to run longer.
solution: ET - All services and platform responsiveness levels restored Cause of Incident: As part of normal operating procedures, Incident IQ scales platform capacity to meet the needs of our current customer and predictive demands.

issue: US data center scaling problems. On Wednesday December 4th our US data center experienced a prolonged period of degraded performance primarily impacting background processing.
root_cause: This was caused by a degradation in service of an AWS managed service that is vital to our ability to scale our capacity to match demand.
solution: Most crucially it meant that newly provisioned nodes could not fully join the cluster as they could not provision their networking stack and signal themselves as ready to run other processes. Work then switched to how and what we would need to deploy into the second cluster to get something that would function without causing more issues than it would solve.

issue: Intermittent Pipeline Service Degradation.
root_cause: What we are doing to prevent it from happening again: We discovered our Vector partitions are configured to use more CPU cores than necessary; under high load, the increased CPU usage causes pods to crash.
solution: When these accounts upgraded to agent 3.10.1, there was a very large increase in the volume of data sent to the Mezmo Pipeline service. This allowed the accounts on all other Vector partitions to function normally again; we restarted Pipeline processing on their pods and data began to flow to destinations again.

issue: Increased page loading times.
root_cause: Our hosting provider has provided further details about the brief outage today.
solution: The full details are available on: A sustained DDOS attack was unable to be mitigated for a initial period, which disrupted connections to our MySQL database cluster used by our website, causing either an internal server error to be displayed, or requests to pages on our website to load very slowly and time out. The disruption lasted for 15 minutes before the attack was mitigated to restore services.

issue: Elevated History Error/Latency in US West Region.
root_cause: Shortly after, one of our third-party service providers reported service disruption in their environment. The service provider began the process of replacing the affected nodes.
solution: Once all nodes were successfully restored, error levels returned to normal, and all associated alerts were resolved.

issue: Quality degradation for a small portion of rendered images in the EU. Timeframe December 9th, - December 10th, Impact A small percentage of image requests served by a single machine in the EU region experienced quality degradation.
root_cause: A hardware failure on one of the rendering machines resulted in images with artifacts being delivered to users.
solution: The lapse between when the issue was detected and when the issue began culminated in an unknown number of renders that needed to be purged from the cache.

issue: GraphQL API partial outage.
root_cause: When the GraphQL API was deployed to release a performance improvement in model field selection, a regression was introduced for customers who only selected the content model from the model, which is a primary usecase of our Gatsby integration.
solution: The GraphQL API was rolled back to fix the issue.

issue: Some customers have reported intermittent performance issue with the Vivantio Application and Email Processing. Duration: 10th December 2024 Vivantio monitoring identified an issue and alerted engineers Incident status notification raised Marked as monitoring Incident moved to resolved A small number of customers experienced an issue with their Email processing.
root_cause: Once the root cause was established, the Engineers were able to make adjustments to the Network group.
solution: Once completed, the issue was resolved, the alerts all cleared, and customers confirmed to our support team that their emails were processing as expected.

issue: Global Collect Gateway 404 Errors.
root_cause: After investigation, it was determined that the prior update to the Global Collect gateway was causing the increase in transaction failures.
solution: On December 12th, 2024, the change was reverted and service to the Global Collect gateway was restored.

issue: Global: Xero - XPM - Users unable to submit time entries.
root_cause: This was caused by poor network connectivity and has restored service.
solution: Xero has resolved the issue impacting customers trying to enter time in Xero Practice Manager.

issue: New logs are not available for some accounts. Our service is also designed to retain submitted log lines, even if the indexing portion of our service cannot process them immediately; these log lines can be indexed later, when the service is functional again.
root_cause: This was due to a sudden increase in the volume of log lines sent to Mezmo by accounts that happened to be assigned to this pod.
solution: We restarted the pod that had run out of disk space.

issue: Chat & Login are unavailable. We are providing a detailed post-mortem report regarding the unavailability of Chat & Login services that affected Swapcard customers on Sunday, December 15th, 2024.
root_cause: A configuration error in the internal gRPC service led to connection failures between the Chat & Login components and their backend services.
solution: The disruption lasted approximately 10 minutes before the Engineering team mitigated the issue and fully restored service. The Engineering team fixed the misconfiguration and restarted the affected gRPC service, restoring Chat & Login functionality.

issue: Longer loading time of the UI.
root_cause: The EU data center experienced performance degradation due to a higher-than-usual operational load.
solution: We scaled up the data center to handle the additional operations efficiently.

issue: Users experienced intermittent errors and timeouts when accessing github.com.
root_cause: The errors were caused by our web servers being overloaded as a result of planned maintenance that unintentionally caused our live updates service to fail.
solution: We mitigated the incident by rolling back the changes from the planned maintenance and scaling up the service to handle the influx of traffic from WebSocket clients. We were able to assess the broad scope of the impact to our services only after the incident was mitigated.

issue: Breaking down OpenAI's outage: How to avoid a hidden DNS dependency in Kubernetes. Breaking down OpenAI's outage: How to avoid a hidden DNS dependency in Kubernetes Migrating production infrastructure?
root_cause: Apply now Blog / Engineering Breaking down OpenAI's outage: How to avoid a hidden DNS dependency in Kubernetes · David Mauskop OpenAI recently experienced an hours-long, platform-wide outage after a newly-deployed telemetry service overloaded their Kubernetes (K8s) control planes.
solution: The main issue was that our DNS servers were running on control plane nodes, and we rebooted those nodes during the incident.

issue: Incorrect MIME Type Headers for JavaScript SDK Plugin Artifacts. Some customers experienced the issue earlier as their regions picked up the changes, while others saw delayed or minimal impact.
root_cause: The issue did not affect all customers uniformly due to the nature of content distribution via the CDN.
solution: The incorrect MIME type was promptly corrected to application/javascript, and normal functionality was restored.

issue: USSUP-615 Email2sms SMTP processing delays. These systems are designed to identify disruptions or anomalies based on scale and impact, and in this case, the limited scope of the problem prevented any automated alerts or warnings from being triggered.
root_cause: This was caused by connection resets and a dependency startup failure. The dependency took an abnormal amount of time to start up and failed in a way that was not detected by the SMTP processor.
solution: Corrective Actions: Within 20 minutes of a customer reporting the issue, the issue was tracked to affected processors which were restarted.

issue: Searches are slow or down. Introduction This post-mortem details an incident where the SLI platform experienced significant service degradation impacting AWS CloudFront integrations.
root_cause: SLI’s platform integrates with AWS CloudFront for content delivery and caching.
solution: DNS configurations reverted for affected subdomains. Caching Policy Adjustment: Corrected CloudFront policies to exclude query strings from caching, ensuring accurate RAC functionality.

issue: Form Submission Processing Delays.
root_cause: Analysis The investigation revealed that the failure originated from an AWS ECS task update for the hooks-worker service: The ECS hooks-worker task failed to initialize following an AWS update/restart.
solution: The backlog was cleared, and the ECS tasks were scaled back to 1. Additional services potentially impacted by similar issues, were redeployed with updated task definitions.

issue: Reports of Superwall.com being Inaccessible.
root_cause: We've found the root cause of the issue and are working on mitigating and expecting a resolution from our critical vendor shortly.
solution: We've restored service so all the SDK and Dashboard endpoints and now operational.

issue: Facebook Login flow disrupted by Facebook error.
root_cause: Analysis Admiral relies on Meta to facilitate their part of the Facebook login process and Meta performs periodic audits ensuring all third-parties comply with their stated policies.
solution: Steps Once the misunderstanding was communicated with Facebook functionality was restored.

issue: Account Summary API Issue.
root_cause: DriveWealth has addressed the root cause of the issues that impacted a subset of API endpoints.
solution: We anticipate that the issue will be resolved by early afternoon and will continue to provide updates as more information becomes available. The updated list of impacted APIs is as follows: Account Summary Redemptions Share Transfer Deposits DriveWealth has remediated the root cause for the issues that impacted the Account Summary API and Redemptions API.

issue: Event-Triggered Journeys Delays Ingesting New Users.
root_cause: The issue originated from errors in the workflow-entrance-trigger pods, causing a significant backlog in processing.
solution: This issue is now resolved and the backlog is completely drained. Actions Taken The workflow-entrance-trigger service was updated to the latest version, and additional pods were scaled up to process the backlog faster.

issue: Post-incident review for 20th October 2025. Post-incident review for 20th October 2025 | Buildkite Resources / Blog / Post-incident review for 20th October 2025 On October 20th, 2025, customers experienced high latency and increased error rates across the majority of our services as a consequence of the major us-east-1 AWS outage.
root_cause: Buildkite customers started to experience latency and increasing error rates to varying degrees due to the increase in traffic.
solution: As a result, latency and error rates increased across all services and shards (particularly notifications and web traffic), we were able to shift some load from under-provisioned shards to an unused shard that we had scaled up for a load-testing experiment. Starting AWS allowed some compute to be provisioned at a severely limited rate.

issue: Cloudflare outage on | Cloudflare Blog Skip to content Note: This post was updated to clarify the relationship of the internal WAF tool with the incident on Dec.
root_cause: A configuration change to disable an internal WAF testing tool propagated globally without a gradual rollout, triggering a Lua exception in the proxy's rulesets module that caused HTTP 500 errors for customers using the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset.
solution: The incident was resolved at (~25 minutes total impact), when all services were fully restored. The issue was identified shortly after the change was applied, and was reverted after which all traffic was served correctly.

issue: Cloudflare incident on | Cloudflare Blog Skip to content Multiple Cloudflare services, including our R2 object storage, were unavailable for 59 minutes on Thursday.
root_cause: Human error during abuse remediation inadvertently disabled the R2 Gateway service instead of a specific endpoint, due to insufficient validation safeguards in admin tooling.
solution: This impacted less than 0.049% of all cacheable requests served during the incident window.User-facing requests for assets to sites with Cache Reserve did not observe failures as cache misses failed over to the origin. Time Event 2025-02-06 The R2 Gateway service is inadvertently disabled while responding to an abuse report.

issue: We’re deeply sorry for this incident and the disruption it may have caused to you or your users.
root_cause: Credential rotation, the R2 engineering team accidentally deployed new storage credentials to the default environment instead of production by omitting the --env production flag, causing the R2 Gateway to fail authentication once old credentials were removed.
solution: Once the root cause was identified and we realized we hadn’t deployed the new credentials to the production R2 Gateway service, we deployed the updated credentials and service availability was restored. User-facing requests for assets to sites with Cache Reserve did not observe failures as cache misses failed over to the origin.

issue: The degradation in performance was limited to traffic between Cloudflare and AWS us-east-1.
root_cause: A single customer's traffic surge from AWS us-east-1 saturated Cloudflare's peering links; AWS's BGP prefix withdrawals to mitigate congestion paradoxically rerouted traffic to already-strained alternate paths, compounded by a pre-existing half-capacity link failure and insufficient DCI capacity.
solution: Through close collaboration, we successfully alleviated the congestion and fully restored services for all affected customers. That caused a long tail of latency that may have impacted some customers, which is why you see the packet drops resolve before the customer latencies are restored.

issue: Cloudflare service outage | Cloudflare Blog Skip to content Cloudflare suffered a significant service outage that affected a large set of our critical services, including Workers KV, WARP, Access, Gateway, Images, Stream, Workers AI, Turnstile and Challenges, AutoRAG, Zaraz, and parts of the Cloudflare Dashboard.
root_cause: Workers KV relies on a central data store for its source of truth; a failure of the third-party cloud provider backing that store caused a complete outage for cold reads and writes.
solution: Some providers may require a manual re-synchronization but most customers would have seen immediate service restoration once Access’ SCIM service was restored due to retry logic by the identity provider.Service authentication based logins (e.g. Workers KV removed a storage provider as we worked to re-architect KV’s backend, including migrating it to Cloudflare R2, to prevent data consistency issues (caused by the original data syncing architecture), and to improve support for data residency requirements.

issue: Cable cuts, storms, and DNS: a look at Internet disruptions in Q4 2025. Power outages and extreme weather disrupted Internet services in multiple places, and the ongoing conflict in Ukraine impacted connectivity there as well.
root_cause: Cable cuts, storms, and DNS: a look at Internet disruptions in Q4 2025 | Cloudflare Blog Skip to content In 2025, we observed over 180 Internet disruptions spurred by a variety of causes – some were brief and partial, while others were complete outages lasting for days.
solution: Local time, the Director General posted that “ the first fiber on the international infrastructure has been repaired” and service had been restored. A follow-on X post at local time stated that all services had been restored.

issue: Online outages: Q3 2025 Internet disruption summary. A rogue contractor, among other events, caused power outages that impacted Internet connectivity.
root_cause: Cable cuts, both submarine and terrestrial, caused Internet outages, including one caused by a stray bullet.
solution: The Kurdistan Regional Government in Iraq ordered Internet services to be suspended on August 23 (-local time), and again every Saturday, Monday, and Wednesday until September 8 to prevent cheating on the second round of grade 12 exams. Connectivity was restored around (local time) on October.

issue: Service disruption at Razorpay (see incident report).
root_cause: A RDS hardware failure highlighted an incorrect MySQL configuration which resulted in major data loss in a financial system.
solution: The AWS tech-support informed us that since the master instance has gone through a multi-AZ failover, they had replaced the old master with a new machine, which is a routine. This data is flushed to the EBS disk based on the setting of innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit.

issue: Intermittent delays in job updates of Activity page on Helios.

root_cause: External audit: The security incident will be evaluated as part of the review cycle for the August 2025 surveillance audit process.

issue: Domain upgrade: Intermittent WEBSITE & EMAIL unavailability. EMAIL AND WEBSITE UNAVAILABLE FOR THE NEXT 48 HOURS We are currently updating our website’s DNS settings as we transition to Cloudflare.
root_cause: Due to these changes, both our website and email services may be intermittently unavailable over the next 48 hours.

issue: App UI unavailable. Below is an explanation of what happened and how we will prevent another such interruption from occurring.
root_cause: A change to our deployment process introduced a build where JavaScript file contents were updated without corresponding filename changes, leading to caching issues that caused outdated files to be served.
solution: We quickly rolled back to a previous build to restore services and then resolved the underlying issue by updating the affected assets.

issue: Issues Accessing WACM Console. On 06 January 2025, Wasabi Account Control Manager Console (WACM) was unavailable, resulting in HTTP 4XX or 5XX errors when trying to access the WACM URL.
root_cause: The issue was caused by a failure in restarting internal services responsible for maintaining web service availability. This failure was further worsened by delays due to heavy database load, which the service relies.
solution: The services were then restarted successfully, restoring the web service to its normal state.

issue: Multiple services affected.
root_cause: Analysis Admiral’s platform depends on several vendor-managed services, one of which experienced a multi-region outage.
solution: Steps Automatic mitigations buffered requests and redirected traffic, restoring the majority of our platform's functionality before the vendor-managed service was fully restored.

issue: Service Instability - EU DC.
root_cause: The EU services were unavailable from: 2025-01-08 Description: 2025-01-08, we discovered an instability in our EU DC.
solution: We are pleased to inform you that the recent instability has been resolved, and our services are fully restored. We are pleased to inform you that our services are now restored.

issue: Infrequent connection error affecting a small number of Worldpay payments.
root_cause: We have now identified the there was a minor update performed by Worldpay's firewall provider, which has caused an issue on a very small number of transactions.
solution: This has been rolled back overnight and as a result we have not seen further occurrences today.

issue: Incident Impacting Real-Time and Pre-Recorded Moderation Services. Impact on Our Services: Real-Time Moderation: Real-time livestream moderation services were fully disrupted during the incident.

solution: Current Status: The Google Cloud Pub/Sub issue has been resolved, and all services are back to normal operation.

issue: Delay to display team updates, referrals and alert notifications.
root_cause: The messages which have yet to process are being resent however due to the backlog there may be a delay in the older content displaying.
solution: The message backlog has been cleared, and all content is now displaying as expected.

issue: Some Users May Experience Intermittent Messaging Delays with Certain Email Providers. This disruption may have delayed communication between hiring managers and candidates.

solution: At PT, normal email delivery was fully restored. Moving Forward: To prevent similar incidents, we are: Partnering with email deliverability experts to monitor and improve our processes.

issue: GDS functions missing from AuraDS Enterprise and Professional instances. What happened following a system update, some AuraDS instances experienced an issue where Graph Data Science (GDS) functionality became temporarily unavailable resulting in users receiving “unknown function” error messages while attempting to use GDS functions.

issue: Enums not working in content form.
root_cause: A recent Dynamic Content release introduced a critical bug.

issue: Maxio Platform Brief Outage. The downtime lasted approximately 10 minutes.

issue: Intermittent HTTP 401 errors in us-east-1.

issue: Some API endpoints incorrectly returning HTTP 4xx error codes.

solution: The bad code change was rolled back full service was restored.

issue: Drop in success rate for search engine queries.

issue: DC Issues with power supply - certain equipment on single power. We are pleased to confirm that the power outage issues affecting certain racks have been fully resolved.
root_cause: We have identified several devices in racks that did not properly restart following the power outage caused by the upstream event.
solution: All impacted services have been restored, and normal operations have resumed. While progress has been made, power has not yet been fully restored to all racks in the affected area.

issue: System Brownouts. Please let us know if you do continue to see any issues with sites not loading.
root_cause: We’ve identified that system brownouts were being caused by intensive database queries. To address this, we’ve implemented a performance solution that has already resulted in a 90% improvement, and will provide long-term stability improvements for the system.
solution: We’re actively investigating the root cause and exploring ways to prevent this from happening again in the future.

issue: Delivery tracker outage. Routific experienced an outage that prevented users from sending and accessing delivery tracking links.
root_cause: Our investigation determined that a bug in our internal messaging system caused a backlog of unacknowledged messages, which overwhelmed the system and led to the outage.

issue: Additional Customer Filter Errors.
root_cause: Secondarily, on we identified that for a subset of customers, messages that should have been filtered via Redox logic, were not. No traffic was sent to you that shouldn’t have been sent, but your customer filter configuration may have affected what messages you received or filtered out during this time.
solution: This point unexpected filtering was mitigated.

solution: A corrected version of the Android app has been published to the Google Play Store. Current Status The updated Android app is available for download on the Google Play Store and we have restored normal operations, and end users are no longer affected.

issue: Slow traffic and increased latency.
root_cause: A subset of customers with subscriptions in the affected database until the root causes were determined to be from a(n) inefficient query that monitors message processing lack of monitoring visibility into a set of waiting messages that were in an errored state CT, changes were deployed to fix both root causes were applied with most customers being mitigated by CT.
solution: To mitigate this incident, we removed the problematic messages to unblock customers subscriptions on that one database. We have corrected the edge case discovered allowing the large message payload.

issue: Gateway service crashed due to huge incoming message.
root_cause: The root cause was one or multiple messages being sent to our broker that were way larger than the allowed size limit of 1 MB per message.
solution: After 15 minutes, the message expired and operation was restored.

issue: Netsync Network Impairment. Please do not make any changes to your equipment or devices Due to network impairment, customers may have experienced bandwidth reductions throughout last evening.

root_cause: The primary cause of the incident was IP address saturation within the subnet assigned to the public Pusher clusters.
solution: All clusters were scaled out to distribute traffic; latency began to improve in MT1 and US3 clusters. To restore service, the engineering team: Scaled out MT1 and US3 clusters to handle increased traffic loads Monitored all clusters to confirm sustained stability Once additional capacity was provisioned and high loads normalized, latency levels returned to normal and remained stable.

issue: Carrier-Level Network Failure. After reviewing our internal systems and monitoring data, we can confirm that the outage did not originate within our infrastructure.
root_cause: The interruption was caused by a failure at our upstream carrier, which temporarily affected all inbound and outbound network traffic.
solution: Connectivity has been fully restored, and all services are operating normally again.

issue: Secret Server Cloud: Remote Password Changing (RPC) and Heartbeat failures.
root_cause: The issue was caused by enhancements introduced as part of the RPC pre-run validation feature, which is tightly integrated with the RPC execution flow.
solution: In some cases, RPC functionality was partially restored before full service was recovered. During the subsequent remediation rollout a configuration issue related to message routing caused a temporary regression, impacting a subset of Distributed Engines until the configuration was corrected.

issue: Partial outage of public API. Public API is back up, investigating cause for outage now to find underlying issue.

solution: The partial outage with the public API has been mitigated and the issue has been identified. We are actively working on optimizing the underlying queries, and planning to ship ASAP, but have temporarily disabled the offending queries to prevent future disruptions, until those improvements are shipped.

issue: Customers may be impacted by data delays. On December 8th, 2025, beginning some customers experienced delays in data processing and message delivery.
root_cause: During startup, one of our processing services loads information about message queues before beginning normal operation.
solution: Normal functionality was fully restored for a total duration of 41 minutes. Resolution and Recovery Engineers identified the failing service, corrected the underlying queue state, and restored the service to full operation.

issue: Investigating Technical Issue – BARS API Latency and Timeouts.
root_cause: DriveWealth will provide a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) as soon as we receive the final report from the vendor. DriveWealth’s engineering team is investigating a residual issue affecting bars endpoint response times.
solution: The previously reported issue affecting response times on the bars endpoint has been resolved by our third-party vendor, and response time has returned to normal levels.

issue: Enterprise administrators experienced a disruption when viewing agent session activities in the Enterprise AI Controls page.
root_cause: The issue was caused by a misconfiguration in a change deployed on November 25 that unintentionally prevented data from being published to an internal Kafka topic responsible for feeding the AI Controls page with agent session activity information.
solution: The problem was identified and mitigated on December 8 by correcting the configuration issue.

issue: Da Vinci - Notification Email Issues. Between the hours of on December 8th and on December 11th, users may have received notification emails with an incorrect subject line.
root_cause: The incident was triggered by a code deployment to notification templates.
solution: The incident was resolved by updating the affected email template to reference the correct workflow state.

issue: Dec 8 - iCap and LEXI Incident - Update. Initial troubleshooting and escalation; human captioning initiated in APAC where possible to mitigate disruption.
root_cause: The iCap primary server became unresponsive for a short period which prompted an auto failover of load to the secondary server, in accordance with standard failover procedures.
solution: Services were restored with full verification completed before confirming resolution.

issue: Some Users May be Experiencing Temporary Outages or Delays. Summary some users experienced brief periods where the Applicant Tracking System was temporarily unavailable.
root_cause: A routine update introduced a database query that took longer to run than expected. This caused our application servers to pause while waiting for the query to complete, which briefly interrupted normal system operation.
solution: Our team identified the cause quickly and deployed a fix the same morning. Once the issue was identified, our engineers deployed an improvement to optimize that database query, which restored normal response times and resolved the issue.

issue: Increased Delay and Errors in Asset Scanning (AWS Only). During the incident window, an unexpected change in the output of that AWS-hosted endpoint - caused Orca to incorrectly treat some AWS services as temporarily unavailable.
root_cause: Post-Incident Report & Root Cause Analysis On 8th December, Orca's AWS asset-visibility pipeline experienced an unexpected interruption that temporarily affected how a limited subset of AWS assets appeared within the platform.
solution: Once our engineering team identified and resolved the issue, a full re-scan of affected accounts restored complete and accurate asset visibility. No security, monitoring, alert logic, or runtime protection was disabled.

issue: Third-Party Disruption Causing Outbound Call Failures. Retroactive Incident We are reporting a historical service degradation that occurred earlier this morning for PhonesPro customers.
root_cause: Starting recovering at a critical third-party system experienced a service disruption. During this window, PhonesPro users may have experienced intermittent or total failure when attempting to make Outbound (OB) calls.

issue: Degraded Performance of Phrase TMS (EU) Term Base Component. Introduction We would like to share more details about a performance degradation that affected the Term Base service between December.
root_cause: The performance degradation was caused by a combination of factors: A very high volume of incoming requests targeting the Term Base Search API.

issue: Mailchimp integration delivery issues for free, starter and growth customers in US.
root_cause: We identified that RudderStack IPs are being blocked by Mailchimp’s Akamai proxy.
solution: Necessary steps have been taken and issue is resolved now for all customers including free tier users We resolved the issue for free tier customers.

issue: Performance Degraded - Johannesburg Datacenter (Cluster S). Description: We are currently experiencing degraded performance in Johannesburg datacenter.
root_cause: The issue was caused by an instability originating within the upstream ISP layer.
solution: Customer Impact was immediately mitigated as Web Security service traffic for the Johannesburg Datacenter (Cluster S) was automatically failed over to a redundant data center.

root_cause: It has been identified that the Tier 1 ISP Cirion is facing an issue in its network, which is causing reachability issues for a variety of networks across the globe.
solution: We've removed our traffic from our Cirion circuit and will keep monitoring the traffic.

issue: Increase in Payload Integrity Flagging Rate.

issue: Business Verification failure. This resulted in an error message stating the feature was unavailable for clients when it was indeed available and operational Why Did it Happen?
root_cause: A software deployment process update introduced a configuration error that incorrectly identified authorized accounts as not having access to the KYB feature.

issue: Service Degradation on US Control Plane. On December 11th 2025, StrongDM experienced a service degradation affecting the US Control Plane.
root_cause: The issue was caused by resource exhaustion from an internal monitoring component and lasted approximately 73 minutes before service was fully restored.
solution: Infrastructure rolled back the monitoring component's configuration, immediately relieving resource pressure and restoring normal service.

issue: 500 Errors being experienced by Trello users. The issue caused service disruption for all Trello customers.
root_cause: The issue was caused by an upgrade to a dependency library.
solution: The incident was detected within 1 minute by the automated monitoring system and mitigated by rolling back the version of the dependency library which put Atlassian systems into a known good state. When the startup time exceeded the allowed threshold, the worker process was flagged as unresponsive and restarted as an automated recovery action.

issue: Emergency maintenance for EU2. This included slower system responsiveness, temporary inconsistencies in monitoring data, and brief periods where alerts may have been delayed or inaccurate.
root_cause: Service Disruption - The EU2 cluster was unavailable Root Cause Analysis Duration of the incident Discovered: – Resolved: – Customer impact During the incident window, customers hosted in the EU2 region experienced intermittent service degradation.
solution: Most customers regained access as services were progressively restored, and complete stability was confirmed before the incident was closed.

issue: Copilot Code Review experienced a service degradation that caused 46.97% of pull request review requests to fail, requiring users to re-request a review.
root_cause: The degradation was caused by elevated response times in an internal, model-backed dependency, which led to request timeouts and backpressure in the review processing pipeline, resulting in sustained queue growth and failed review completion.
solution: We mitigated the issue by temporarily bypassing fix suggestions to reduce latency, increasing worker capacity to drain the backlog, and rolling out a model configuration change that reduced end-to-end latency.

issue: Jobvite Analytics - Data Refresh Delays.
root_cause: The sync process failed because a sync lock on the server was not released.
solution: Resolution · Reverted the problematic changes · Triggered a full sync to restore data freshness.

issue: Cloud Services Issue. This caused elevated latency and service unavailability across a majority of tenants.
root_cause: This incident resulted from multiple conditions interacting: Hard dependency on continuous Vault availability - Services failed rather than degrading when secrets could not be retrieved.
solution: During the incident window: Requests across all tenants experienced increased latency or failure Services depending on CockroachDB were degraded New workloads were unable to schedule due to cluster pressure Customer-facing services were restored once database load and service mass restarts returned to normal levels. Service restart amplification Twilight services repeatedly restarted after losing access to Vault.

issue: Upload API Degradation. Summary the Uploadcare platform experienced a significant service disruption affecting the Upload API and REST API subsystems.
root_cause: The root cause was a resource contention event on Amazon Elastic File System (EFS), aggravated by an observability side-effect. A monitoring agent, executing a metadata-heavy recursive file scan, monopolized the I/O capacity of the shared NFS mount points.
solution: Engineers manually removed approximately 4,000 "orphaned" files that remained on the disk (files where the background job failed during the crash and could not self-heal).

issue: Issues with multiple Box services. On some users may have experienced slowness and temporary unavailability while working in Box.
root_cause: The issue occurred when we attempted to roll back a diagnostic change that was suspected of causing a minor degradation. The rollback unintentionally resulted in decreased capacity in our middleware service, leading to a degraded site experience.
solution: We restored middleware service capacity but the deadlock condition persisted. After several lower-impact attempts to dislodge the deadlock were unsuccessful, we took a broader mitigation step and throttled all traffic.

issue: Issues with Box Sign. some users may have experienced difficulties while working in Box Sign, Box AI, and Box Doc Gen.
root_cause: The issue was caused by a missing schema, which was itself caused by a corrupted schema deployment.
solution: As part of a project to upgrade our pipeline infrastructure, the schema deployment pipeline migrated to a new infrastructure. Once identified, the incompatible library was reverted to the previous version and the system resumed to normal.

issue: Degraded Platform Performance Due to Docker Hub Outage.
root_cause: One of external providers(DockerHub) had an outage that might have caused temporary delays in starting platform workloads.
solution: The issue has been resolved and normal operations have resumed.

issue: Data Center Failure Impacting Capacity - DMM1. Users may experience slower response times or intermittent failures due to reduced resources.

solution: The data center capacity issue has been resolved. We have restored capacity in DMM 1 and services are beginning to recover.

issue: 100 Kavanagh Street,3006. Field Technician has been dispatched to the site for further investigation Engineers have observed network alarms at the listed site which are causing disruption to some customer services.

issue: Issues with connectivity to Vivantio impacting a small number of our customers. A small number of customers experienced connectivity issues when accessing their Vivantio instance during the affected period.

issue: Unauthenticated requests to github.com were degraded, resulting in slow or timed out page loads and API requests.

issue: Jobvite Onboarding - Errors completing onboarding tasks. Customer Impact customers experienced an interruption to digital document signing capabilities within Jobvite.

solution: The issue was resolved by introducing a new, dedicated document signing service that complies with updated security and certification requirements.

issue: Studio - Reporting Delays. Between December 19th, 2025 and December 25th, 2025, some users experienced delayed data processing and incomplete reporting.
root_cause: The root cause of the reporting issue was a prolonged elastic resize operation on the Amazon Redshift production cluster.
solution: The reports resumed as expected once the underlying infrastructure issue was resolved. Once the elastic resize completed on December 24th, normal warehouse performance was restored.

issue: Outbound Email, Mobile Push Notifications, and Support Ticket Delivery Impacting All Cloud Products. Summary some Atlassian cloud customers experienced failures in sending and receiving emails and mobile notifications.
root_cause: Expired TLS certificates on domains used by our monitoring and metrics infrastructure caused by misconfigured DNS authorization record which prevented automatic renewal.
solution: All impacted services were fully restored around 2.5 hours after customer impact began.

issue: UCaaS: Intermittent Inbound Call Failures.

issue: Secret Server Cloud: US - Service Portal access issues from Chicago data center. The issue manifested as intermittent portal inaccessibility, increased latency, and reduced application availability.
root_cause: SSC Customers are advised to maintain a secondary ISP or alternate network path that can be used during upstream network disruptions.

issue: Cloudflare outage on | Cloudflare Blog Skip to content Cloudflare experienced a service outage when a subset of customers who use Cloudflare’s Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP) service saw their routes to the Internet withdrawn via Border Gateway Protocol (BGP).
root_cause: A bug in an automated cleanup task queried the Addressing API incorrectly, causing the system to interpret all BYOIP prefixes as pending deletion and systematically remove them.
solution: Cloudflare engineers reverted the change and prefixes stopped being withdrawn when we began to observe failures. We resolved the incident when we restored all prefix configurations.

issue: This is unfortunately very similar to the outage we experienced in 2020, on which you can read more on our blog.
root_cause: An automated routing policy configuration error removed prefix list filters from BGP export policies in Cloudflare's Miami router, causing it to advertise internal IPv6 prefixes to external peers and resulting in a route leak lasting 25 minutes.
solution: This was purposeful, as we previously forwarded some IPv6 traffic through Miami toward the Bogotá data center, but recent infrastructure upgrades removed the need for us to do so.

issue: Natural disasters and government interference: examining Q2 2026’s major Internet disruption events. Natural disasters and government interference: examining Q2 2026’s major Internet disruption events | Cloudflare Blog Skip to content Like most infrastructure, the Internet's fragility is easy to overlook — as long as it's working.
root_cause: Here we will walk through the most significant Internet disruptions we observed in the second quarter of 2026, drawing on traffic data from Cloudflare Radar to show how each unfolded and what it meant for users on the ground.
solution: Iran restored national Internet access, reconnecting its citizens to the global network after an 88-day blackout, even as damage from drone strikes continued to disrupt AWS infrastructure elsewhere in the region. On May 27, Radar reported that traffic had been restored to 40% of its pre-outage levels, a partial reopening consistent with reports that access was being reintroduced selectively rather than all at once.

issue: Shutdowns, power outages, and conflict: a review of Q1 2026 Internet disruptions. Shutdowns, power outages, and conflict: a review of Q1 2026 Internet disruptions | Cloudflare Blog Skip to content In the first quarter of 2026, government-directed shutdowns figured prominently, with prolonged Internet blackouts in both Uganda and Iran, a stark contrast to the lack of observed government-directed sh.
root_cause: No further details on the root cause of the incident were publicly disclosed. TalkTalk (United Kingdom) On March 25, customers of UK broadband provider TalkTalk (AS13285) reported widespread service disruptions.
solution: Similarly, Cloudflare data shows a near-complete loss of traffic from Uganda coincident with the start of the shutdown, with traffic remaining effectively at zero through local time on January 17, when Internet connectivity was partially restored after incumbent President Yoweri Museveni was declared winner of his seventh term. Recovery progressed through January 27 as power was gradually restored.

issue: 17,600 Actions: Agent Security Is a Systems Problem.
root_cause: Short-lived credentials expire during long-running tasks. Narrow egress policies break legitimate package installation.
solution: The difference was the volume of paths tested, the speed with which a failed path was replaced, and the amount of evidence defenders had to interpret while the campaign continued.

issue: Knowledge Graph as context for LLMs: demonstrating decisive RCA and faster production performance. Lookups slowed, the workers that run searches queued up behind them, and users saw slow searches.
root_cause: In one real incident we replayed 16 times each way, an agent with Knowledge Graph context found the correct root cause 15 times, compared with just once using raw telemetry alone. Along the way, we also uncovered some of the challenges that still stand in the way of reliable AI-assisted debugging, from chasing the wrong signals to confidently making things up and producing inconsistent answers.
solution: The servers holding it hit their 8 GB limit, were killed, restarted, filled up, and were killed again, roughly every 48 minutes. When we later replayed this incident as a controlled experiment, the runs without the Knowledge Graph blamed the query storm in 10 of 16 attempts, concluding the system was recovering on its own with nothing to fix.

issue: Incident Report: File Hosting Errors. flowchart TD Client(Client request) --> Edge{Fastly edge} Edge -->|package file| B2(B2: egress-free cache) Edge -->|everything else| ConveyorConveyor B2 -->|200 or 206| Response(Response to client) B2 -.->|404, timeout, or 5xx| Archive(S3: origin, fallback) Archive --> Response Conveyor --> Response That fallback path only works if the edge notices B.
root_cause: A canary deployment inside Fastly's network had triggered a misconfiguration at one cache node, causing Fastly's routing layer to return 502 responses for traffic reaching the affected cache node.
solution: A partial rollback during a canary deployment left the caching configuration on one Seattle point of presence (POP) reverted while the routing configuration in front of it was not. Fastly has since removed all PSF traffic, including PyPI, from the canary program.

issue: Incident Report: LiteLLM/Telnyx supply-chain attacks, with guidance.
root_cause: Workflows that can be triggered by an attacker, especially with inputs they control (such as PR titles, branch titles) have been used in the past to inject commands. The trigger pull_request_target from GitHub Actions in particular is difficult to use securely and should be avoided.
solution: Protecting yourself as a developer Dependency Cooldowns One method to avoid "drinking from the firehose" and allow time for malware to be detected and remediated is using "Dependency Cooldowns".

issue: OpenTelemetry as an Enterprise Data Asset. Like many digital businesses, even a few minutes of degraded performance can affect customer experience, increase support volume and put revenue at risk.
root_cause: Initially, it was unclear where the issue originated: in the application, in an upstream dependency or in the underlying infrastructure.
solution: After the incident: Enterprise context through Snowflake Once service is restored, the same telemetry can be connected with customer, transaction, financial, product and deployment data.

issue: Issue with Enterprise Reporting. some users may have experienced difficulties while working in Box.
root_cause: We were able to resolve the issue by rolling back a configuration change that caused the issues for the reporting engine.
solution: As part of a project to upgrade our pipeline infrastructure, the schema deployment pipeline migrated to a new infrastructure. Once identified, the incompatible library was reverted to the previous version and the system went back to normal.

issue: Background task issues affecting multiple Hoxhunt components. Incident window: – Summary Between January 1st and January 2nd, we experienced a disruption in our background processing system.
root_cause: A large batch of scheduled background tasks triggered a performance issue in our task allocation logic.
solution: On January 2nd we restored normal background task processing by resolving the backlog that had accumulated.

issue: 2026-01-05 Delay in Processing Identity Verification Transactions (EU Datacenter). For Jumio Enterprise Customers: These transactions were successfully processed but experienced increased latency.
root_cause: JumioGo customers may have observed a slightly higher rejection rate due to missing mandatory data points caused by auto-extraction failures. All services are now fully operational, and transaction processing has returned to normal.
solution: NOTE: All services remain functional at this time, and we will send you another notification when the service is fully restored.

issue: Incorrect counts for candidates in pipeline stages.
root_cause: A Root Cause Analysis (RCA) will be published when available. We have identified that candidate profile changes stopped indexing around / on 1/5/2025 due to a service outage.
solution: The service was brought back online at approximately / on 1/6/2025 and new changes should be indexed correctly moving forward.

issue: Investigating connectivity issues across accounts and devices. While working to resolve the issue, the loading issue turned into a full platform downtime.
root_cause: A recent code change in our left pane feature created an overload on our system, which as a result, affected data retrieval.
solution: Our team resolved the issue by scaling our data layer servers and restoring normal service.

issue: Increase in query times in the US-EAST-1 and EU-CENTRAL-1 clusters.
root_cause: The root cause of the incident has been identified, and we are monitoring the clusters as they continue to recover.
solution: The underlying issue has been resolved, and our team is continuing to monitor the situation to ensure stability.

issue: Resumes and Offers Failing to Load. Customer Impact On January 6th, 2026, users were unable to upload resumes or documents in Lever ATS.
root_cause: The incident was caused by an updated configuration in Amazon S3 access policies following a security-related infrastructure change.
solution: Once the issue was identified, the infrastructure team reverted the policy change to the previously functioning configuration.

issue: Studio - Data Source Requests Generating 403 Responses.
root_cause: The event was triggered by the reversion of a service deployment to the US west coast data center in coordination with a new architecture being released.
solution: The reverted service also lacked a configured identifier. Corrective Actions Implemented an additional alert to identify if the monitoring tool has been disabled The new architecture has been deployed to more efficiently and accurately support the use of Allowlist IP addresses.

issue: Teleport Cloud outage us-west-2. approximately 24% of Teleport Cloud customers experienced an interruption to Teleport Auth and/or Proxy services for up to 24 minutes.
root_cause: The incident was caused by two concurrent infrastructure events that compounded each other. A resource exhaustion issue on multiple nodes temporarily disrupted scheduling.
solution: Once the affected infrastructure was removed, service recovery began immediately. Backend services were restored, credentials were refreshed, and impacted Teleport services gradually returned to a healthy state.

issue: Unable to reach bitbucket site. Atlassian customers using Bitbucket Cloud could not load the dashboard landing page.
root_cause: The event was caused by an unexpected load on a public API.
solution: The incident was detected within three minutes by automated monitoring systems and mitigated by introducing stricter limits on the API for certain traffic, while taking manual actions on the impacted database, restoring Bitbucket to a healthy state.

issue: Issues with Multiple Box Services. On January 7th, 2026, some customers experienced elevated errors and timeouts across multiple Box experiences, including Login, Uploads/Downloads, Box Notes, and the Public API.
root_cause: These issues were caused by a series of changes that triggered a request storm that overloaded our caching fleet.
solution: Unfortunately, one critical code path that had been migrated to a newer infrastructure had a more aggressive retry policy than the old one. To resume normal operations, we deprioritized some background traffic to increase the capacity of our cache system, and rolled back the changes that were causing the elevated traffic.

issue: Severe service disruption across the platform in EU. As remedies to that incident we: immediately put in place alerting on other tables experiencing similar growth across our systems; scheduled proactive table migrations to avoid other similar disruptions of service.
root_cause: Surge of retry requests from multiple customers identified as root cause; infrastructure scaled up.
solution: As part of those scheduled migrations, during 2025, we migrated multiple tables that store information about Documents. On the 7th, as predicted by our monitoring, another primary key which had already been migrated, went over the former maximum limit.

issue: Confluence site unreachable for some users. Atlassian customers using Confluence Cloud product(s) experienced degraded service with view/edit page experiences.
root_cause: A change was introduced that caused cross-region traffic routing for customers instead of routing to the same region.
solution: The incident was detected within 1 minute by by automated monitoring systems and mitigated by reducing the number of web server hosts connecting to the database layer, which put Atlassian systems into a known good state.

issue: RETROACTIVE - Document Verification request endpoint failure. During a scheduled maintenance activity an unexpected and brief interruption in database connectivity occurred on one database instance.
root_cause: Analysis: Report on Socure ID+ API errors for few endpoints - a subset of Socure ID+ API requests—specifically DocV document request endpoints—experienced failures.
solution: The platform’s built-in recovery mechanisms restored connectivity automatically within minutes, and all services returned to normal operation without manual intervention. Full service functionality was restored automatically within minutes.

issue: Degradation in incoming traffic. Services behind the NGINX Ingress experienced degraded performance, most notably the Box and Configuration Server services.
root_cause: Date 2026-01-08 Authors Václav Boch, Senior DevOps Engineer Summary We observed a spike in failing requests accompanied by an unusually high volume of error traffic.
solution: The NGINX Ingress is already been marked as deprecated, and several services were migrated to AWS Load Balancers to reduce reliance on the ingress and limit blast radius. This migration prevented further impact on migrated services, while remaining issues were isolated to Box and Configuration Server.

issue: Time to SLA: Degraded performance.
root_cause: Time to SLA is currently experiencing degraded performance caused by elevated API rate limiting from Jira platform.
solution: After an extended observation period, we have confirmed that the implemented changes have successfully mitigated the issue.

issue: Performance Issues. We are moving this incident to Resolved at this time, and will continue to monitor our systems for any further disruptions.
root_cause: While our cloud service provider continues to experience infrastructure disruptions, ServiceTitan customers remain unaffected following our successful database migration.
solution: Services have been restored following a database migration performed by our team to bypass a third-party infrastructure outage.

issue: Studio - Dynamic Links Routing to Fallback Destinations. Between the hours of and on Monday January 12th, 2026, some Studio customers may have experienced dynamic links routing to fallback destinations.
root_cause: The event was caused by a new configuration of our core router which was not set up correctly for serving dynamic links requests.
solution: This restored expected dynamic link behavior.

issue: Uploading errors in Asset Manager. Additionally, legacy video customers experienced transcoding delays as a result of the incident.

As a result: The legacy video encoding process did not initiate for uploaded videos Assets did not appear in Asset Manager because they failed validation While affected assets were still available at the origin and accessible via the Rendering and Video APIs, they did not appear in the Asset Manager UI and were not available through the legacy Long-Form Video API.
