solution: Cytracom Engineering has identified the issue impacting voice services for a subset of customers and has applied a fix. Customers should begin seeing normal call behavior restored.

issue: Elevated error rates from API.
root_cause: One of our autoscaling groups controlling the API fleet had a misconfiguration that caused targets to drain and not replenish.
solution: The errant configuration was identified and corrected and full service was restored in minutes.

issue: GitHub Copilot experienced a service outage with error rates averaging 18% and peaking at 100%.
root_cause: The incident was triggered by a configuration error introduced during a model update and was initially mitigated by rolling back the change.
solution: We have completed a detailed root‑cause review and are implementing stronger monitors, improved test environments, and tighter configuration safeguards to prevent recurrence and accelerate detection and mitigation of future issues.

issue: Da Vinci - Platform Experiencing Syncing/Proofing Issues. Between the hours of ET and ET users may have experienced issues with syncing or proofing in Da Vinci.
root_cause: This was caused by one of our email send monitor tasks becoming stuck, which prevented any other ESP sync related tasks from being processed.
solution: More workers were manually provisioned to allow for the ESP sync tasks to resume being processed. Between ET and ET the backlog of queued ESP sync tasks was cleared and service returned to normal.

issue: 2026-January-13 Service Incident. The App Storage Service experienced high response times in the US-West-1 datacenter.
root_cause: Due to a high number of concurrent uploads, the App Storage Service experienced increased connection latency and delays in acquiring connections to the backend.
solution: Service was restored by restarting the application.

issue: Intermittent Authentication Issues for AWS EU-CENTRAL (read/write token authentication is not affected). Additional customers reported the same errors.
root_cause: Cause of the Incident The incident was caused by the clock on some of the nodes being slightly behind the master clock.
solution: Recovery We identified the nodes whose clock time had drifted, and drained the affected nodes. When the service was restarted on new nodes with the correct time, the problem was resolved.

issue: Performance Disruption of Phrase Portal (EU). During this time, users were unable to access the portal.
root_cause: The issue occurred when the platform’s traffic routing infrastructure reached a fixed capacity limit on the number of active service associations it could manage.
solution: Service was confirmed fully restored and the incident was marked as stable. Improved Alerting Alert thresholds for routing capacity have been adjusted to ensure earlier visibility and to elevate urgency before reaching critical limits.

issue: RSA ID Plus Service Incident <EMEA Region>. On –, a subset of customers hosted on the EU1 deployment in the EMEA region experienced a degradation in authentication services.
root_cause: A January service update introduced a flaw in our upgrade handling which caused some clients to unnecessarily retrieve application resources, creating unexpected request patterns within the authentication flow.
solution: Mitigation and Recovery Actions During the incident, the following actions were taken: Rolled back January service updates deployed prior to the incident Scaled additional capacity within the affected EMEA deployment Continued real-time monitoring to validate stabilization These actions successfully stabilized the environment.

issue: Business Verification vendor failure.
root_cause: While our automated monitoring systems detected the error rate spike immediately, the resolution required intervention from the provider's engineering team, which extended the duration of the incident.
solution: The provider has rolled out a fix, and services are fully restored. We have backfilled the missing data for affected businesses.

issue: Data science feature on AuraDS, AuraDSE and Aura Professional tiers - Native projection affected.
root_cause: What happened we began rolling out an update that included an incompatible version of a key component, affecting customers using the GDS plugin.
solution: This issue was reported on January 16 and a fix was deployed within hours, restoring functionality for the majority of affected users. Although a corrected package was created and labeled separately, the release pipeline selected the incorrect package for deployment.

issue: Degraded Deep Search performance.
root_cause: We identified an edge case in how Deep Search processes streaming events. As a precautionary response we have temporarily turned this off for Sourcegraph Cloud customers.
solution: The issue has been resolved The issue has been fully resolved. All Sourcegraph Cloud customers have been upgraded to the patched version.

issue: Investigation Ongoing Into Delayed Observation History on Some Devices.
root_cause: Under normal conditions, the system processed device observations without issue.
solution: We want to provide a transparent overview of what happened, how we responded, and the steps we are taking to prevent this from happening again. The backlog was fully cleared and all historical data is now current.

issue: Partial Service Disruption- API Key Error. Partial service disruption due to 401 Error with Unauthorized API Key.
root_cause: Between PT and PT, developers experienced minor service disruption due to API Key Error.
solution: The issue has been identified and resolved, normal service operation is restored.

issue: Advanced Billing: Intermittent HTTP 500 Errors on Product Catalog & Subscription Endpoints (Third-Party Exchange Rates Outage).
root_cause: Between 2026-01-17 and 2026-01-17 Advanced Billing merchants using exchange rates experienced intermittent HTTP 500 errors on the Product Catalog and Subscription API endpoints due to a third-party service disruption with Open Exchange Rates.
solution: This was mitigated on our end as of 2026-01-17, and service is operating normally.

issue: Limited payment options available for some regions. Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) options such as Klarna will remain temporarily unavailable for affected regions (SEK, NOK, DKK, CZK) until Open Exchange Rates fully restores service.
root_cause: Specifically, we found Krone (SEK, NOK, DKK, CZK) based currencies were primarily impacted. As Open Exchange Rates continues to resolve the issue we fully expected our systems to perform as expected.
solution: Open Exchange Rates has restored service and currency conversion is now functioning normally. We have deployed a fix to ensure checkout pages load correctly while Open Exchange Rates continues to experience issues.

issue: Sanity CLI init flow regression.
root_cause: On January 20th there was an update to the Sanity CLI that had a regression when trying to run the init flow (npm create sanity@latest) that resulted in a non-functioning project.
solution: This update was rolled back at January 21st at ~2am.

issue: Issues with accessing Vivantio impacting a small number of customers.
root_cause: During the standard deployment process, one of the web servers in the region encountered an issue before completing the rollout, which created a cascading failure that ultimately impacted all web servers and resulted in a temporary regional outage.
solution: Our engineering team restored service and successfully re-deployed the change, then continued monitoring to confirm stability.

issue: KernelCare NFS Freeze on CL8/EL8.
root_cause: A KernelCare adaptation of the CVE-2025-39697 NFS patch introduced a locking regression. Specifically, the patch caused the same spinlock to be acquired twice within a single execution path: - nfs_page_group_lock - nfs_page_group_sync_on_bit This resulted in a deadlock that left kernel threads stuck in the D state.
solution: Once triggered, the patch could not be safely unloaded, and affected systems either froze indefinitely or rebooted due to hung task watchdogs.

issue: Document Reports not being processed in US. Summary around 10 minutes after restoring service in the EU and CA from the - outage, we go alerted for high error rate in the US region and we noticed the new ML model version was back online in that region.
root_cause: A previously rolled back version of an ML model went back live automatically in the US region. The automated canary reversal did not succeed in that region, leaving the deployment in an inconsistent state.
solution: As a result, the model routing labels were not updated as expected during the next forced deployment, and traffic continued to be served by pods running the incorrect model version until we manually rolled back the model in the cluster.

issue: Email Processing Delays Due to Microsoft Outage - US.
root_cause: As of on January 23, Abnormal's Inbound Email Security services have fully recovered from the processing delays due to the widespread Microsoft outage.
solution: Microsoft has confirmed that access to Microsoft Defender for Office, Microsoft Purview, and DNS functionality has been restored, and Exchange Online mail flow remains stable. Microsoft has reported that while they have restored their affected infrastructure to a healthy state, additional load balancing is required to mitigate persistent impact from the earlier outage that began.

issue: Asana webapp unavailable. Incident: On 2026-01-22 the Asana App and all associated services had a service disruption due to dependency on a shared database used for storing metadata.
root_cause: This was triggered by a code path which caused overload for that database, followed by request queuing, timeouts, and errors.
solution: Moving forward: We immediately rolled back our application code and added resources for this database.

issue: High Rate of Transaction Drops and Transaction Inclusion Delays.
root_cause: The root cause was a configuration change to how transactions were propagated between our mempool nodes and the block builder.
solution: Our Learnings and Next Steps We are taking immediate and long-term actions to prevent this type of incident from recurring and to improve our response. We have validated the fix restored overall network stability.

issue: Give access is not working on US region.
root_cause: A limited number of customers experienced delays in permission grants Permission requests were processed later than expected No data loss occurred No incorrect permissions were granted No security impact was identified Root Cause The issue was caused by a temporary backlog in background job processing in the US region, which delayed execution of permission requests.
solution: The underlying issue was resolved at restoring normal service. Our engineering teams mitigated the issue by: Releasing delayed background jobs Scaling processing capacity to clear the backlog Verifying successful permission grants Service functionality was restored.

issue: Problems With Fastly API Could Cause Stale Content to Be Served to Customers in Some Regions.
root_cause: Ultimately, the issue stemmed from an error that prevented entities from being deleted in a given database table.
solution: All of the failed deletions were manually cleared, and now cache purging works as intended.

issue: Automation Workflow Trigger Delays. Customer Impact Between January 21, some customers experienced delays in automated workflow execution.
root_cause: We had a single instance that had accumulated a very large number of automation workflows configured to trigger on the same event type.
solution: Service levels were fully restored workflows have been operating in real time since that point. These changes significantly reduced system load, allowed processing queues to catch up, and restored real‑time workflow execution.

issue: Da Vinci - Salesforce Marketing Cloud Degraded Performance. Between the hours of Salesforce Marketing Cloud experienced a service outage.
root_cause: Once identified, our team cataloged affected campaigns, validated that the root cause was upstream, and continuously monitored Salesforce's incident updates.
solution: We coordinated with CX to support client outreach and provided updates as Salesforce restored service across stacks.

issue: Incorrect subscription changes affecting some accounts.
root_cause: We’ve been made aware of an issue caused by our billing provider, Maxio, where a limited number of our customer accounts were incorrectly downgraded due to an incident on their side.
solution: All affected accounts have been restored to their correct subscription levels.

issue: Degraded service functionality or unable to access multiple Microsoft 365 services. User Users may be seeing degraded service functionality or be unable to access multiple Microsoft 365 services.
root_cause: A portion of dependent service infrastructure in the North America region isn't processing traffic as expected.
solution: Current status: While Microsoft has restored the affected infrastructure to a heathy state, further load balancing is required to mitigate persistent impact.

issue: PennO365 Service Degradation. All email sent during the outage was queued and delivered.
root_cause: The root cause of the issue was identified as lack of capacity due to maintenance on a portion of their infrastructure.
solution: Microsoft resolved the issue at around eastern and PennO365 is functioning normally. Services are returning to normal, but it will take some time for full functionality to be restored.

issue: 1Password Browser Extension Code Syntax Rendering Issue. Impact on Customers Customers experienced broken code-block syntax highlighting on websites with HTML elements while using the 1Password browser extension version 8.11.22 across all major browsers.
root_cause: Analysis: We did not have an enforced dependency boundary for injected content scripts, which allowed unexpected UI and runtime dependencies to be bundled into the page-injected context.
solution: We removed PrismJS from the scripts the extension injects into web pages by eliminating the import chain that pulled it into the injected bundle. Fix was applied to the previous stable release.

issue: Data duplication anomaly detected.
root_cause: A routine data processing run, we identified an issue where some data records were duplicated. This duplication may affect the accuracy of certain data-dependent services, including: Cloud Exports Insights platform data (on insights.hoxhunt.com) We have taken steps to prevent further data corruption in future processing runs and are now actively working to assess and correct any impacted historical data.
solution: We are thoroughly investigating the root cause to prevent recurrence and are verifying the integrity of all related systems.

issue: Secret Server Cloud: US - RDP/SSH Connectivity Issues. Incident Overview Customers in the US region experienced intermittent failures when initiating RDP and SSH sessions through Secret Server Cloud, specifically via the Connection Manager / RDP proxy.
root_cause: As part of a planned maintenance activity in the US region on January 23, customer-facing Azure Service Bus resources were migrated to new hostnames, along with updates to email services and domains.
solution: To avoid data loss and disruption to active customer sessions during the maintenance: A replica set of compute nodes continued to point to the legacy Service Bus A new set of compute nodes were provisioned to use the new Service Bus hostnames This temporary configuration required approximately double the normal compute capacity, which is not a typical operating condition.

issue: Temporary Reviews Feed Unavailability. We experienced a brief global incident that caused the reviews feed to be unavailable for a small number of users.
root_cause: A database connection limit was reached due to a MySQL configuration issue.
solution: This immediately removed the bottleneck and restored normal operation.

issue: Document report processing disrupted in EU. On 26 January 2026, our document reports processing was severely degraded with customers experiencing extended processing time to about 85% of their traffic.
root_cause: A core service for fraud prevention on documents came under elevated load, causing kubernetes pods to go down in quick sequence.
solution: On-call engineers manually increased capacity for the impacted document fraud‑prevention service.

issue: Performance Disruption of Phrase TMS (EU) Project Management component 10 AM. Introduction We would like to share more details about the events that occurred which led to a performance disruption of the Phrase TMS (EU) Project Management component.
root_cause: The disruption was caused by exhaustion of available database connections in the LQA service’s underlying production database.
solution: Some service instances restarted due to repeated failures.

issue: Email Security Cloud - Advanced Encryption Service Un-available.
root_cause: We identified the issue and requested the vendor to revert the applied changes. Description: We are currently experiencing a problem with our external email encryption provider due to which our email security solution is not able to receive an encryption or decryption token from our vendor.
solution: Current Status & Our vendor has reverted the changes, and the problem is resolved We are currently monitoring our environment for stability and will provide a final update once we have confirmation.

issue: Service Degradation - Manual Tasks.
root_cause: The issue was caused by a configuration error in our internal task management system, which prevented it from correctly assigning tasks to our analysts.
solution: We fixed the configuration and restored normal processing by 28 Jan 2026 11h50 AM, and cleared all manual task backlogs by 18h00.

issue: Acquia has detected a service degradation affecting Cloud UI metrics. We are currently investigating an interruption of metrics reporting within the Cloud Platform user interface.
root_cause: This is due to a connectivity issue with our backend metrics provider. Cloud UI: Customers may experience difficulties accessing or viewing real-time metrics and historical performance charts.
solution: Connectivity with the backend metrics provider has been restored, with metrics ingestion working correctly and performance charts loading as expected in the Cloud UI.

issue: Cloud Connector Asset Cleanup Delay.
root_cause: We identified a scaling issue that caused a backlog in the cleanup of outdated cloud connector assets in some workspaces. Configuration changes have been applied and the system is now actively processing and removing stale assets.
solution: The backlog of outdated cloud connector assets has been fully cleared.

issue: VerifySession_Fail" error pops up for users with eChat permission. Summary our eChat service experienced an intermittent disruption that impacted user communication and system stability.
root_cause: The incident was caused by an incorrect system configuration.
solution: To resolve the incident, our DevOps team redeployed the eChat service with the correct production configuration. This fresh deployment cleared the invalid settings and restored the necessary connections between our internal components.

issue: We’ve identified an issue with our email service.
root_cause: The email delivery delays were caused by a system issue that led to an unexpected spike in outbound email volume.
solution: The issue has been resolved, and all services are now operating normally.

issue: Email events and workflow enrolment delayed.
root_cause: We are mitigating impact from a database impairment which we believe is caused by resource exhaustion. The information on this page reflects our understanding of the incident and impact at the time of the update.
solution: We're resolved the issue causing event processing delays since ( -).

issue: Da Vinci - Proofing and Syncing slowness. Incident Summary users experienced issues with campaigns failing to progress through Proof Runner, in some cases, campaigns reverting from syncing back to draft.
root_cause: The issue was triggered by an unintended platform permission change that temporarily disrupted access to a backend messaging service responsible for processing audience queries, proof generation, and creative syncing jobs.
solution: Even after the underlying issue was corrected, the accumulated backlog contributed to continued slowness until normal queue processing levels were restored. At the unintended permission change was identified and reverted, restoring normal access to the affected backend service.

issue: Performance Disruption of Phrase TMS CAT Web Editor and Project Management (EU).
root_cause: During a deployment, session storage was migrated to a new caching solution.
solution: Actions to Prevent Recurrence Treat session storage changes as planned maintenance and communicate them in advance.

issue: 2026 - January - 29 Resolved Service Incident. We are working to implement processes to handle periods of increased load and proactively detect performance degradation to implement automated remediation and self-healing capabilities.
root_cause: Application uploads and automated tests in the US-West-1 data center experienced intermittent errors Due to a high number of concurrent uploads and a temporary change to the network topology schema, the App Storage Service experienced increased connection latency and delays in acquiring connections to the backend.
solution: App Storage Service network topology schema was restored to its original state.

issue: Checkout Service Degradation. Summary a subset of customers experienced checkout errors.
root_cause: This incident was caused by an internal deployment issue that temporarily affected checkout service behavior.
solution: The situation was mitigated through manual intervention, restoring normal service levels.

issue: Outage affecting 'Log in with Email'. Incident Report: Login By Email Service Outage - January 30th, 2026 CloudVision as-a-Service experienced a service outage affecting the "Login By Email" functionality lasting 2 hours and 36 minutes.
root_cause: Our investigation identified a gap in monitoring for a critical third-party integration.
solution: We are committed to implementing changes identified during our internal investigation to prevent this type of failure from happening again.

issue: Collaborate (EU) - Intermittent join issues.
root_cause: Friday, / - A small subset of Collaborate users may have temporarily experienced issues joining sessions due to an AWS CloudFront distribution issue.
solution: The issue was resolved, and service continues to operate as expected.

solution: Clients may notice minor discrepancies in analytics data from approximately – ET, which will be automatically backfilled later today.

issue: Dependabot service was degraded and failed to create 10% of automated pull requests.
root_cause: This was due to a cluster failover that connected to a read-only database.
solution: We mitigated the incident by pausing Dependabot queues until traffic was properly routed to healthy clusters. All failed jobs were identified and restarted.

issue: GitHub Actions hosted runners and GitHub Codespaces were unavailable, with service degraded until full recovery at for standard runners, at for larger runners, and February 3 at for codespaces.
root_cause: This outage was caused by a loss in telemetry that cascaded to mistakenly applying security policies to backend storage accounts in our underlying compute provider.
solution: This was mitigated by rolling back the policy changes, which started.

issue: ISAAC-ORI Cluster Unavailable.
root_cause: The ISAAC-ORI cluster is unavailable due to a fiber optic cable cut between UTK and ORNL.
solution: Service to the ISAAC-ORI cluster has been restored.

issue: Issue with Payments. During this period of the incident, end‑users were unable to successfully initiate one‑time or bulk payments.
root_cause: Analysis Following a detailed investigation, it was determined that the incident was caused by an availability issue affecting a critical database table.
solution: Follow-up actions To prevent similar issues in the future, Tink will be implementing the following actions.

issue: Workspot Control Experiencing Intermittent Availability.
root_cause: A detailed Root Cause Analysis (RCA) will be shared once available. Following the rollback performed, no new issues have been reported.
solution: The service has been fully restored after the rollback was performed. Engineering team has completed the rollback, and all services have now been successfully restored.

issue: Confluent Cloud Service Outage. During the incident, some Kafka clusters experienced intermittent connectivity issues, and some control plane services, including metrics, logging, authentication, and new cluster provisioning, were briefly impacted.
root_cause: The root cause was a networking configuration change in the us-west-2 region that caused client connection issues starting at resulting in intermittent service disruption across several Confluent Cloud services, including Kafka, Flink, Metrics API, Logging, Provisioning, and Authentication.
solution: The issue has been resolved and services are operating normally. The change was reverted, and as of, services have been fully restored.

issue: Degraded performance for some users. AEST, We became aware of the issue following customer reports of system slowness.
root_cause: The root cause of this incident was an ongoing service issue within Microsoft Azure that affected storage accounts used by VM custom extension packages.
solution: AEST All systems were fully restored and operating normally.

issue: Dashboard transaction processing delays. Our transaction processing infrastructure in the EU region experienced degraded performance due to database connectivity issues.
root_cause: The issue was triggered by increased load on our storage infrastructure combined with inefficiencies in our data access patterns.
solution: Successfully processed all delayed transactions with no data loss The backlog was fully cleared and all transaction data became available in customer dashboards.

issue: Vanta web app temporarily unavailable.
root_cause: The Vanta web app was unavailable (17 minutes) due to a configuration change related to a third-party vendor outage.
solution: This change has been rolled back and the incident is now resolved. The changes are being rolled back and service should be restored soon.

issue: Duplicate continuous emails sent to attendees.
root_cause: Analysis The root cause was an incorrect assumption in the delivery-history lookup logic: The deduplication check queried a datastore that only contained delivery records populated starting 2025-02-04.
solution: 2026-02-04 | The change was reverted, stopping further duplicate sends. We resolved the incident by reverting the change introduced at 2026-02-04, restoring the previous behavior and preventing additional duplicate emails from being sent.

issue: Elevated GIT/Application Builder Errors. Delta generation service experienced degraded performance from ~0900 Feb 4 to ~1700, due to 32-bit address space limitations affecting large image delta processing.
root_cause: Delta generation timeout rate increased significantly for large container images Users experienced slower image deployments and potential timeouts No data loss or security impact Worker auto-discovery began routing some large delta generation tasks to 32-bit Docker sockets, causing memory constraint failures.
solution: Corrected worker selection routing to only use 64-bit sockets for delta generation.

issue: Intermittent platform availability. Users may have seen a "temporarily down" message during this window.
root_cause: We identified the issue as resource contention within our database caused by background processing. The site has fully recovered and is operating normally.
solution: To prevent recurrence, we are actively implementing optimizations to our background processing and data request logic.

issue: Degraded Performance of Phrase Orchestrator (EU) Next-Gen Workflow Engine between February 05, and February 05. Introduction We would like to share more details about the workflow disruption that occurred which led to workflows being held in an “Executing” state and delays in workflow processing within Phrase Orchestrator.
root_cause: The incident was triggered by the execution of a very large workflow with a complex dependency structure.
solution: Below we describe what happened, the root cause, and the steps we are taking to prevent similar incidents in the future. Actions to Prevent Recurrence We are taking the following steps to prevent similar incidents in the future: Improved Alerting: We are improving our alerting mechanisms to ensure we are notified more quickly when workflows stop progressing.

issue: App/Intranet German System / US System / Asia/Pacific System - Incorrect Page Update Timestamps.
root_cause: While deploying this configuration change, a system process unintentionally triggered a timestamp refresh for all pages where an update reminder was active.
solution: Our developers successfully identified the cause and reverted the timestamps for all impacted pages by February 5th.

issue: Mendix Cloud EU (Frankfurt) issue sending email using SMTP relay.
root_cause: This issue is caused by one or more of our outgoing IP addresses being blocklisted by an external email security provider.
solution: The affected outgoing IP addresses have been removed from the external email security provider's blocklist. We are in communication with the external email security provider to have the affected IP addresses removed from their list.

issue: System Errors in US-WEST-1 Region. Wasabi’s Operations Team was alerted by our automated monitoring systems that multiple racks were experiencing power disruptions, which impacted customer access and operations during this time.
root_cause: On 6 February 2026 Wasabi S3 services in our Hillsboro (us-west-1) region were unavailable due to a partial power issue within our datacenter facility.
solution: Flexential performed controlled restoration procedures and subsequently replaced the failed breaker under emergency change control. Following power restoration and comprehensive system validation checks by Wasabi’s Operations Team, services were progressively restored and us-west-1 region were fully operational.

issue: Bug in Atlassian Forms API causing issues with new conditional sections.
root_cause: We got an update from Atlassian engineering and they expect the bug to be fixed in "a weeks time".
solution: A fix has been rolled out by Atlassian for the issue.

issue: Partial outage in JFrog Cloud Platform affecting services on Azure US West. Official Microsoft outage details and status updates can be tracked at: We are currently experiencing a partial service disruption affecting customers in the Azure US West region.
root_cause: Status: Resolved / Post-Recovery Validation Services Restored JFrog services are now fully operational following the resolution of a significant upstream infrastructure outage within Azure.
solution: Recovery & Ongoing Validation While primary connectivity and service layers have been restored, the JFrog engineering team remains in an active monitoring phase. Subsequent Window: Azure Cloud services were recovered, enabling the sequential restoration and stabilization of the JFrog service layers.

issue: Kalix Downtime Due To Azure WestUS Outage. Further updates can be seen here: While the power outage has been solved, it seems like the recovery is still underway.
root_cause: The service that is causing the current Kalix outage is experiencing downtime in the West US region of Azure due to a sudden power outage, and this issue is still being worked.
solution: The affected component has just been restored, so Kalix is operational again.

issue: GitHub experienced two related periods of degraded availability affecting github.com, the GitHub API, GitHub Actions, Git operations, GitHub Copilot, and other services.
root_cause: Our investigation determined that both incidents shared the same underlying cause: a configuration change to a user settings caching mechanism caused a large volume of cache rewrites to occur simultaneously.
solution: We mitigated this incident by disabling async cache rewrites and restarting the affected Git proxy service across multiple datacenters. We mitigated by disabling the source of the cache rewrites and again restarting Git proxy.

issue: Platform: Error Message When Navigating Between Pages. Incident Overview Platform users experienced red banner errors, “Cannot access ‘t’ before initialization”, when clicking on the Discovery link in the left-hand navigation.
root_cause: The incident was caused by a minor Angular framework update that indirectly upgraded the webpack to a newer version - a change that was not explicitly requested or anticipated.
solution: Start of Impact, at End of Impact, at Resolution We resolved the incident by pinning our build tooling back to the previous compatible version of webpack, which restored correct bundle generation and eliminated the errors. Normal service was confirmed to be restored.

issue: Trello performance is degraded. Atlassian customers were unable to access Trello.
root_cause: The issue was cause by increased memory requirements during the transition from the weekend to EU business hours, combined with Auto Scaling group scaling rules based on CPU utilization.
solution: Access was restored for paid users approximately 43 minutes after the onset, with full service restoration for free users 10 minutes later. As a result, Trello went down and users received HTTP 502 errors until the incident was resolved.

issue: Restoration of historical data in AWS, US-East-1. During the restoration process, some customers experienced elevated TTBR and degraded query performance while restoration was underway.
root_cause: The change had a bug that, under certain circumstances, caused some data to be dropped during the compaction process.
solution: When compaction completed, the new compacted file (missing a portion of the source data) replaced the original files. This made some data unavailable until it was restored from backup.

issue: Workspace degraded performance. The scan itself was non-disruptive in design and was a platform security procedure, not intended as a customer-impacting maintenance activity.
root_cause: Beginning at a subset of Workspace instances across multiple regions became slow or temporarily unresponsive due to memory exhaustion on their underlying virtual machines.
solution: To resolve this issue, we identified and progressively redeployed the affected instances, starting with the majority restored shortly after.

issue: EU PhishER Integration Delay. On Tuesday, some users experienced delays with the integration service on the EU instance of the PhishER console.
root_cause: This incident was caused by a system upgrade that unexpectedly affected the integration service, causing errors in the production environment.
solution: To resolve this issue, we reverted the update, and the PhishER console returned to normal performance.

issue: Da Vinci - Issues with Campaign Syncing. Incident Summary there were intermittent outages that prevented campaigns from loading.
root_cause: The event was triggered by a code change that altered the way database connections were handled by the web API used to retrieve campaign information.
solution: The issue was fully resolved at with the deployment of a corrective code change that restored proper database connection handling.

issue: Landis Phone Queues Outage. The Landis outage affecting UVU call centers has been resolved.
root_cause: 3rd party software vendor Landis continues to troubleshoot the call queue outage.
solution: A fix has been applied and calls made to the Enterprise Service Desk, Financial Aid, and Admissions should route normally.

issue: Reports of form notification emails not being delivered. We recognize how disruptive this issue is for customers who rely on this functionality, and we remain engaged with our upstream provider to resolve the issue and restore normal notification delivery as soon as possible.
root_cause: Due to an issue with an upstream provider, Form submission notification emails were not processed as expected between February 10th - February 11th.
solution: Form notification email functionality is now restored and our upstream provider are now processing these emails as expected.

issue: Elevated Cloudlink Errors.
root_cause: The Cloudlink servers were using an expired certificate that was due for replacement.
solution: The certificate has been replaced, and Cloudlink servers were restarted to use the new certificate.

issue: MS Teams Conferencing Failures. We have seen that our error rate provisioning MS Teams Conferencing has returned to normal, low levels since yesterday.
root_cause: We believe the root cause is a lack of generated URLs for a meeting when we call Microsoft Graph APIs.
solution: Some conferences are being provisioned after automatically retrying, but still not as many as we'd expect.

issue: Service Disruption. Incident Summary some Prismic customers experienced difficulties logging in and accessing their repositories.
root_cause: These issues were caused by a DNS resolution failure on AWS CloudFront, one of the infrastructure providers Prismic relies.
solution: AWS identified the root cause and progressively restored normal operations.

issue: App access problems. Following the release of iOS version 5.41.8, some users experienced authorization errors that affected access to certain app features.
root_cause: An issue introduced during the app update impacted authentication for a subset of users.
solution: Users were not fully blocked, and access could be restored by signing out and back in. A corrected version of the app was expedited through App Store review, approved on Friday and verified in production.

issue: Intermittent Provider Issues. Note that while you may see interruptions in connections your audience may not.
root_cause: We have received reports of intermittent DNS resolution issues on bit.ly due to residual caching from a recent provider outage.
solution: We are working with affected ISPs to get the erroneous DNS entries cleared from their residual cache layers.

issue: Average, the archive download error rate was 0.0042% and peaked at 0.0339% of requests to the service.
root_cause: This was caused by the deployment of an incorrect network configuration in the LFS Service that caused service health checks to fail and an internal service to be incorrectly marked as unreachable.
solution: We mitigated the incident by manually applying the corrected network setting. Additional checks for corruption and auto-rollback detection were added to prevent this type of configuration issue.

issue: Da Vinci — Web App Inaccessible. Incident Summary multiple components of the Da Vinci Web App experienced degradation.
root_cause: This was caused by a database migration that inadvertently locked a table containing key campaign information.
solution: The deployment process was cancelled and the migration was aborted, which released the database lock and restored normal platform functionality.

issue: SwapAccess issue in badge printing. We are providing a detailed post-mortem report regarding the service disruption that affected Swapcard customers on February 12th, 2026.
root_cause: Analysis The root cause of this incident was an unprecedented and sudden spike in concurrent traffic that exceeded the scaling capacity of one of our internal services.
solution: The platform progressively recovered as request queues cleared. Badge printing and Studio access returned to normal operation.

issue: All-in-One: Native E-signature Experiencing Errors.
root_cause: Native e-signatures are non-functional in Ashby due to an issue with an upstream provider. Ashby may display a success message, but the upstream provider will not be able to complete the e-signature process.
solution: The issue has been resolved by the upstream provider. Until service is restored, customers will need to use our DocuSign integration or an e-signature service outside of Ashby.

issue: API Disruption. API Disruption During the night of 2026-02-14, our public API experienced a significant disruption across all instances of the service, impacting major API-driven integrations.

issue: Edu-ID authentication issues. Incident Postmortem: SAML Edu-ID Login Outage Incident Summary | Field | Details | | --- | --- | | Date | – | | Duration | 7 days | | Severity | High — complete SAML Edu-ID login unavailability | | Affected System | Keycloak SAML Edu-ID authentication (Renku realm), Renkulab 2.15.0 | | Status | Resolved.
root_cause: Analysis Starting with Keycloak version 21 (introduced in Renkulab 2.14.0, deployed ), Keycloak stopped decrypting SAML assertions that were encrypted using a realm key originally generated for signing purposes.

solution: We'll continue to post updates here until the issue has been resolved.

issue: Intermittent errors from Platform and Search. Censys Engineering is continuing to remediate degraded behavior in search queries.

issue: And (lasting 4 hours and 16 minutes) we had two incidents, where the Copilot coding agent service was degraded and users experienced significant delays starting new agent sessions.
root_cause: This was due to a bug in our rate limiting logic that incorrectly applied a rate limit globally across all users, rather than scoping it to the individual installation that triggered the limit.
solution: We mitigated the incident by disabling the faulty rate limit caching mechanism via feature flag and updating our service to use per-installation credentials for API calls, ensuring rate limits are correctly scoped to individual installations.

issue: WhatsApp Inbox experiencing an outage. Users may have experienced errors or degraded functionality on the Inbox platform during the upgrade window.
root_cause: The issue was caused by a database migration dependency conflict during the upgrade process, which has been resolved.
solution: The Inbox platform has been successfully upgraded to a new version. All functionality has been restored An issue affecting access to the WhatsApp inbox has been identified.

issue: Degraded Performance in Orchestrate. immediate mitigation was completed by scaling up Orchestrate service resources, stabilizing the system and stopping further degradation.
root_cause: The issue was identified as being caused by a retry mechanism repeatedly processing failed jobs. These failures stemmed from oversized payloads (~6 MB) generated in custom actions, which exceeded Kubernetes API server limits, leading to continuous retries and added strain on the system.
solution: Additional safeguards, including payload size limits and an upcoming SDK fix, were prepared to prevent recurrence.

issue: Notifications to Pagerduty, VictorOps, Slack, Webhook, Microsoft Teams and OpsGenie are not delivered.

Webhook notifications will be reprocessed and delivered at a later date.

issue: Users experiencing issues with login across Atlassian products. Summary customers experienced failures when attempting to log in, sign up, reset passwords, and complete multi-factor authentication flows across Atlassian cloud products.

solution: The incident was mitigated within 40 minutes through manual intervention, and full service was restored. The incident was mitigated by manually scaling up the downstream identity service to provide sufficient capacity to absorb the amplified load.

solution: Service returned to normal and the incident was fully resolved.

issue: Increased function execution latency.

issue: API Performance Degradation. A backend optimization deployed on April 24 inadvertently triggered a database performance issue that caused a platform-wide outage.

That authorization check relied on an existing database query with significant hidden complexity: under normal conditions it goes unnoticed, but at production policy-check volume it joined approximately 2 million rows per call, taking around 25 seconds to complete.
solution: The change has been fully reverted and the platform is stable. The optimization was fully reverted, restoring normal platform behavior.

issue: When DNSSEC goes wrong: how we responded to the.de TLD outage. When DNSSEC goes wrong: how we responded to the.de TLD outage | Cloudflare Blog Skip to content at roughly, DENIC, the registry operator for the.de country-code top-level domain (TLD), started publishing incorrect DNSSEC signatures for the.de zone.
root_cause: A break anywhere in that chain causes validation to fail for everything below it, which is why a misconfiguration at a TLD like.de affects every domain under it.
solution: In this post, we’ll walk through what we saw, the impact of these events, and how we applied temporary mitigations while DENIC resolved the issue. As a precautionary measure, future rollovers have been suspended until the exact technical causes have been identified.” We're sure we’ll hear more when their own analysis is ready.

root_cause: We identified a subset of customer session failures in our Realtime SaaS - US region.
solution: Our team has restored the service to normal performance levels.

issue: Issues with Box Shuttle Standalone.
root_cause: Analysis A misconfiguration in Shuttle resulted in depleted resources that accessed job history. This caused Shuttle pages that load job history to time out.
solution: After we restored service, we confirmed that customers could access existing jobs and create new ones. We restored access by restarting the affected services.

issue: Harness Artifact Registry upload is failing from pipeline - EU1 region.
root_cause: The component responsible for handling pipeline-based artifact uploads is distributed as a container image.
solution: Because of how that replication was triggered, it copied the original (earlier) image associated with that version label rather than the corrected one. This meant the EU1 cluster — which pulls from the internal mirror — ended up running a different, defective image than other clusters, which pull directly from the public source and therefore received the corrected image.

issue: UI dashboards are lagging behind (CI).
root_cause: Harness maintains a change-data-capture component that continuously replicates pipeline execution records from the primary operational datastore into a separate time-series datastore optimised for dashboards and reporting queries.
solution: Every affected record remained durably stored and was replayed into the analytics datastore once the underlying limitation was removed. Harness migrated the affected clusters to a horizontally scalable, queue-backed version of the replication component on 1 August 2026 and completed targeted data backfills for all affected accounts.

issue: Querying issues. This timeout was not properly communicated back to the lambda, and while with classic lambdas the task would automatically cut off at 15 minutes, the new LMIs were not enforcing this sort of safety mechanism.
root_cause: First, we have been introducing Lambda Managed Instances (LMI) into our query architecture, which behave similar to classic lambdas in many ways and had been introduced as part of work around querying performance improvements with the goal of a better and faster user experience.
solution: The system recovered by CT, 20 minutes later, when the large queries cleared out, but we continued to investigate the cause of the incident.

issue: Interruption to Programmatic Vanta Agent Installations. We have resolved an issue where customers were unable to programmatically install the Vanta agent using our installation scripts (such as deployments via MDM).
root_cause: This was caused by an unexpected permissions change that made the scripts repository private starting.
solution: Full access has been restored, and scripted installations are now functioning normally.

issue: Incident with Copilot AI Model Providers. users of the Fable 5 model in GitHub Copilot experienced increased request failures and latency.
root_cause: This was caused by degradation of an upstream model provider. The affected endpoint recovered, and we monitored the service until error rates and latency returned to normal levels.
solution: The degradation affecting Copilot AI Model Providers has been mitigated.

issue: Flexera One- IT Asset management - EU - Inventory upload and Beacon communication issues. Affected customers experienced failed inventory package uploads, including HTTP 504 (Gateway Timeout) and HTTP 405 (Method Not Allowed) responses.
root_cause: The investigation determined that earliest impact started July 31st, 2026. Analysis identified a communication issue within a critical service routing path that prevented a subset of requests from successfully reaching downstream processing services.
solution: The issue surfaced later, when application components were restarted and began establishing new connections using the updated configuration. Service was restored by redirecting traffic to an alternate communication path that was not affected by the certificate-related configuration issue.

issue: Main DB outage. On the afternoon of, Autentique experienced an outage affecting both the API and web application during a production deployment.
root_cause: The incident was caused by a database schema change executed as part of the regular application deployment process.
solution: Once the database contention was removed, traffic and service availability returned to normal. After identifying the source of the database contention, we stopped the schema change and removed the condition preventing queries from being processed.

issue: Databricks courses may fail to load.

solution: The upstream Azure Databricks issue appears to have cleared and Databricks exercise environments are provisioning normally again.

issue: Inbound connection failure to Fly Apps.

solution: The misconfiguration has been fixed and we are implementing safeguards against this kind of issue in the future.

issue: Incident with Copilot. On 2026-08-03, some GitHub Copilot users experienced errors when using chat and agent features.
root_cause: The incident was caused by an increase in how often clients requested the model list, which pushed an internal user-authorization lookup past a rate limit; the rate-limited responses were surfaced to users as errors.
solution: We mitigated the impact by increasing how long Copilot caches that authorization lookup, which reduced load on the internal service, and we have additional capacity and rate-limit changes in progress. The degradation affecting Copilot has been mitigated.

issue: KPO podspec changes for GPU-enabled nodes may cause KPO pod startup failures.

solution: We have rolled back the changes that triggered this issue and are monitoring the issue for confirmation that this issue is resolved.

solution: Commerce Engineers are investigating an issue impacting PayPal Account Vaulted instrument creation when the Credit Cards feature is disabled in the PayPal Commerce and BigCommerce Payments integrations.

issue: Issues with Uploads and Downloads. On some customers experienced failures and delays when uploading files to Box.
root_cause: The problem was caused by a routing issue on our frontend load balancers.
solution: We restored service by rerouting upload traffic and provisioning additional capacity. Our engineering team mitigated the impact by redirecting traffic away from the affected region, which restored normal upload operations and resolved the errors.

issue: Users are not able to login. At 10 AM, while being investigated by the On Call engineer, customers started reporting that they were unable to access the platform—all pages seemed to be affected.

issue: Flexera Support Cases - Delayed or Failed Email Notifications for Case Updates.

issue: Incident with Actions. on August 7, GitHub Actions experienced degraded availability.
root_cause: The incident was triggered by a routine deployment to an internal Actions service responsible for processing events and generating Actions jobs.
solution: As pods were replaced during the deployment, remaining capacity became saturated, causing services to crash and triggering a cascading impact across multiple clusters and downstream services. This second stage of impact was mitigated by deploying changes to prevent runners from repeatedly attempting to acquire invalid jobs.

issue: As the core services recovered, a latent bug in the job-assignment path made recovery slower: runners were handed jobs that had already been revoked, then got stuck retrying them instead of picking up valid work, which created a self-amplifying backlog.
root_cause: A routine deployment that briefly reduced the number of running pods was enough to exhaust available headroom.
solution: Over roughly the next two hours we expanded capacity for the saturated services and throttled incoming webhook-triggered work so the system could stabilize. We deployed fixes so runners stopped trying to acquire invalid jobs, drained the accumulated queues, and raised the internal rate limits that were slowing recovery.

issue: Monitoring - Pipelines Stuck - Prod2. As each pass consumed progressively more memory and CPU without ever completing, the service instance performing that work stopped making progress, and every execution assigned to that instance stalled — which is what customers reported.
root_cause: Harness pipelines support expressions that are resolved at runtime — for example, an expression that inserts the contents of the Git webhook payload that triggered the pipeline.
solution: Harness engineers identified the cause, mitigated the impact, and pipeline executions returned to normal operation. The majority of pipelines on Prod2 continued to execute successfully throughout the incident; the primary impact was that some in-flight executions could not complete and needed to be re-run once the issue was mitigated.

issue: SEI 2.0 dashboards are not loading. No customer data was lost, and ingestion of all integration data continued to work uninterrupted.

issue: Disruption with Login and Release Asset downloads. There were three windows of (1) August 12, with an average error rate of 16.16% that peaked at 28.6%; (2) August 12, with an average error rate of 16.55% that peaked %; and (3) August 13, with an average error rate of 2.01% that peaked %.

issue: EU (European) Region Service Disruption - Third Party. On September 4th, Act-On customers hosted in our European region experienced disruptions to several services, including outgoing webhooks, CRM sync, Custom Objects, dashboards and reporting, beginning.
root_cause: The incident was caused by a configuration change on our vendor's infrastructure that affected components responsible for authorizing incoming network traffic.

issue: Delayed data processing in the Europe region. Replaying several days of data was the slowest part of the recovery by design, as we rate-limited the replay so that real-time ingestion wasn't put at risk.
root_cause: The cutover multiplied concurrent write streams on the cluster, and the volume of concurrent inserts saturated per-host write throughput on I/O contention.
solution: Our initial fixes, tuning the write path and adding capacity, restored real-time ingestion within a day, but draining the backlog alongside live traffic re-created the contention. We then rebuilt the recovery pipeline and held live data with strict priority while separately replaying the backlog at a controlled rate.

issue: Webhook Notification Delivery Delays and Missing Notifications. Overview Between the afternoon of Thursday 3 September 2026 and the evening of Friday 4 September 2026 (UK time), some customers experienced delays receiving webhook notifications from Currencycloud.
root_cause: The delay was caused by a performance issue in the database supporting our notification delivery system, which caused it to run under sustained heavy load.
solution: The underlying issue was identified, and a fix was deployed on Friday 4 September 2026, and the resulting backlog was fully cleared by the evening of the same day. Once the fix was deployed and the backlog cleared, the large majority of delayed notifications were delivered automatically with no need for any customer action.

issue: Disruption with Copilot Code Review. Affected pull request reviews failed to complete or post review comments.

solution: We reverted the change and restored normal operation.

issue: Degradation in repos contents API. some users experienced errors and elevated latency for repository operations.

solution: We resolved the incident by reverting the change and letting traffic rebalance.

issue: Outbound email delivery – delayed.

issue: Advanced Aggregations — Degraded Performance. On September 4–5, 2026, we experienced an issue affecting Advanced Aggregations in which some customers saw inaccurate aggregation results because recent card transaction data may have been missing.
root_cause: The root cause was a data type mismatch: the cards table id values grew beyond the maximum value supported by a 4-byte integer.
solution: After mitigation was deployed, we replayed the queued events and completed a backfill so that aggregations reflected the correct underlying transaction data.

issue: DBDevOps Builds Failing intermittently. Summary on Wednesday, some customers running Database DevOps pipelines in Production experienced intermittent failures when executing schema migration steps (for example Apply Schema and related Database DevOps steps).
root_cause: This issue required two separate problems to occur together. First, pipeline plan creation runs on a shared pool of background worker threads, and each thread can handle work for many different customer accounts over time.
solution: Immediate: Rolled back the Database DevOps service change that enforced the stricter account-binding validation in the most impacted Production environment, restoring Database DevOps pipeline execution for affected customers.

issue: KSAT - Unable to Login (US Only). After hitting a platform execution limit, the job was terminated and automatically retried five times in 15-minute intervals, resulting in a 75-minute outage.
root_cause: An unbounded, single-transaction background job for large-group user archival held exclusive locks on many affected rows, blocking the login process's own row write.
solution: To resolve the issue, we deployed a fix that decoupled logins from the lock. When the job reached a 15-minute platform execution limit, it was terminated mid-transaction, the transaction rolled back, and the job was redelivered to the queue.

issue: From 40 seconds to under 10: rebuilding incident detection on OpenTelemetry, Apache Kafka, and Apache Flink on Kubernetes. An error rate or a volume drop that a human would call an incident.

issue: Elevated wait times for machine jobs. Between October 1, CircleCI customers experienced five separate incidents in which jobs waited longer than normal to start, or failed to start.
root_cause: One was caused by a configuration issue in our scheduling infrastructure, and one by memory limits on an internal service, which we raised during the incident.
solution: The service that gives each job its configuration at startup ran out of memory and restarted. engineers applied a fix that set up the fast disks correctly.

issue: Scan Performance Degredation. This occurred during a period of high event volume, which led to the database reaching maximum capacity and slowing down the overall processing workflow.
root_cause: The incident was caused by a combination of high event volume and a lack of "fail-fast" logic for permanent errors.
solution: We scaled up our database capacity, increased the number of processing units to handle the higher volume, and implemented logic to stop retrying updates that fail due to permanent permission errors. All backlogs have been cleared, and system performance has returned to normal for all pull requests.

issue: Unprocessed Push Event.2026 and 28.04.2026, a small portion of push events were not processed correctly.
root_cause: The issue was triggered by a change in the update process that attempted to perform multiple database operations simultaneously within the same request.
solution: The issue has been fully resolved, and all affected data has been reprocessed to ensure accuracy, IDT: A subsequent system update was rolled out that inadvertently corrected the processing error.

issue: GitHub Authentication Incident Affecting Cycode GitHub Integrations.
root_cause: The incident was caused by an external authentication failure at GitHub.
solution: The issue was resolved once the external provider restored their authentication services. All integrations have automatically returned to normal operation, and no customer action is required.

issue: GitHub PR Delays. The failures occurred simultaneously across many unrelated accounts and were resolved without any changes on our side, indicating a service disruption on the provider's side.
root_cause: The issue was caused by an external service provider returning "no access" responses during a routine validity check.
solution: Restored expected processing behavior once connection tokens were successfully refreshed.

issue: GitLab Integration — Connection Issue. Summary a temporary issue within our internal processing system interrupted the routine renewal of GitLab access credentials for a subset of integrations.
root_cause: The issue was triggered by a temporary interruption in our internal update process.
solution: Because the affected credentials were no longer valid, they could not be restored from our end — each affected integration had to be manually re-authenticated by the customer in order to resume syncing. As the credential was no longer valid and could not be recovered from our end, these integrations could not be restored automatically and required the customer to re-authenticate.

issue: PR Scans are Delayed. (1/2) Summary some Cycode customers using GitHub integrations experienced interruptions in their development workflows due to issues affecting pull request (PR) status checks and scan execution.
root_cause: The issues on June 30 were caused by a combination of configuration, scaling, and infrastructure limitations.
solution: The image was rolled back and memory limits increased without resolving the issue. It was restarted but remained in “Creating” state.

issue: Connectivity issue in Boden.
root_cause: On-site technicians found the root cause, a fiber/cable break. The traffics have been automatically re-routed to our redundant circuit.
solution: Outage is resolved and services are restored.

issue: Elevated Errors on US-4 Public Cloud.
root_cause: A root cause analysis (RCA) will be posted here within 7 business days. We've identified a load spike event that caused elevated service errors on the US-4 Public Cloud environment.
solution: After monitoring the environment to ensure stability, we confirm that services have been restored.
